events.text: The Celestial Ministries give you a desk in the Ministry of Prayers: a hall so long its far end is in a different season. Every prayer said below arrives here as a slip of paper and waits to be answered. Most have waited a very long time. On your first morning a slip falls off the top of a pile, and the valley it names is the one you were born in.

effects.log: You send a small rain to a field that asked for it a hundred and twelve years ago. Somebody's great-grandchild gets the harvest. (+2 merit)

choices.text: File it in its proper place, as the rules say

effects.log: You file it. It goes to the bottom of a pile that reaches the ceiling. The Ministry approves of you. (+4 merit)
You spend a year counting. The number is so large the clerks ask you not to write it down. (+3 Mind)

events.text: Word has gone round the Ministry that you read the slips. A very old clerk, ink to the elbows, stops at your desk and whispers that there is a back room where the prayers the Court decided never to answer are kept. "For safety," the clerk says, and does not say whose.

choices.text: Ask to see the back room

effects.log: It is full of prayers for the end of wars the Court found useful. You read until your eyes ache. (+4 Mind)

choices.text: Tell the clerk to keep the secret

effects.log: The clerk nods, relieved, and brings you better ink from then on. (+2 merit)

choices.text: Report the clerk for speaking of it

effects.log: The clerk is transferred to the Ministry of Fog. You rise, and the hall goes very quiet when you pass. (+6 merit)

events.text: A minister calls you in. The unanswered prayers, it seems, have begun to weigh on the clouds: the Ministry's hall sinks a finger's width every century. Something must go. The minister proposes burning the back room. Someone else proposes answering it.

choices.text: Speak for answering every last one

effects.log: It takes the Ministry three hundred years, and below, wars end that nobody can explain. The minister never forgives you. (+8 align)

choices.text: Burn them, and spare the hall

effects.log: The smoke smells of ten thousand voices. The hall rises a finger's width. You are promoted for good sense. (+8 merit)

choices.text: Find a third way: let the prayers answer each other

ok.log: You pair each prayer with one that answers it: a drought with a flood, a lonely farmer with a lonely widow. The hall rises. The minister calls it impossible and takes the credit. (+5 merit, +4 Mind)

fail.log: Your matching tangles. Two kingdoms below get each other's weather for a year. The Ministry pretends it was policy. (-2 merit)

events.text: You are posted under the Star Marshal of the West, who has guarded the cloud border against the Demon Realm for eleven thousand years and has the patience of a cliff. One night you find the Marshal alone on the wall, reading a letter sealed with black wax. The seal is a Demon King's.
events.arc: The Star Marshal of the West

effects.log: The Marshal folds it and looks at you a long time. "An offer," the Marshal says. "Old ones are always getting offers." (+2 Mind)
You say nothing. From then on you keep one eye on the Demon border and the other on the Marshal. (+2 luck)

choices.text: Report it to the Court at once

effects.log: The Court thanks you and sends an inspector. The inspector finds nothing; the letter is gone. The Marshal greets you coldly. (+3 merit)

events.text: The Marshal comes to you at the change of watch. "Eleven thousand years," the Marshal says, "and the Court has never once asked whether this war is worth fighting. The Demon King asks." The Marshal means to open the western gate for one night, to talk, and wants you to hold it.
events.arc: The Star Marshal of the West

choices.text: Hold the gate, and stand beside the talk

effects.log: You hold it. The Marshal and the Demon King talk until dawn, and in the morning the war is a little smaller. (+6 align, -3 merit)

choices.text: Talk the Marshal out of it

ok.log: "Not like this," you say, and something in the old face gives. The gate stays shut. The letter goes into a brazier. (+4 merit)

fail.log: The Marshal hears you out and opens the gate anyway, with someone else holding it. You are not invited. (+2 Mind)

effects.log: The Court arrives before the gate opens. The Marshal does not resist. You are made a Star Marshal yourself, which you did not want. (+10 merit)

events.text: Word of the night at the western gate has reached the Celestial Ministries, as word always does. A tribunal is called. The Marshal stands before it with folded hands and names nobody. Then a minister asks, very politely, who held the gate.
events.arc: The Star Marshal of the West

choices.text: Stand up and say it was you

effects.log: The tribunal is so surprised by an honest answer that it adjourns for a century. When it sits again the war has quietly cooled, and nobody wants to be the one to warm it. (+10 align, +30 fame)
The Marshal is stripped of rank and sent to guard a cloud with nothing on it. On the day of leaving the Marshal nods to you, once, without blame. (+4 merit)

choices.text: Argue the case for peace before the whole Court

ok.log: You speak for a day and a night. The Court does not make peace, but it makes a ministry to consider peace, which up here is a revolution. (+6 merit, +40 fame)

fail.log: The Court listens politely, and transfers you to the Ministry of Fog for a decade to think about tone. (-4 merit)

events.text: At the top of the Celestial Ministries there is a throne, and on the throne there has been nobody for nine hundred years. The ministers bow to it every morning and govern by guessing what it would say. This year a faction of ministers decides the throne has been silent long enough. They have a candidate. They would like your name on their scroll.

effects.log: Your name goes on the scroll. Doors open for you that were closed yesterday, and three ministers stop speaking to you. (+5 merit)
You refuse. The faction smiles and remembers. The throne, as ever, says nothing. (+2 Mind)

choices.text: Ask who decided the throne was empty

effects.log: Nobody can tell you. The answer is lost somewhere in nine hundred years of guessing. You start to look. (+3 Mind)

events.text: You find, in the Court's oldest archive, the last order the throne ever gave. It is one line long. It says: "Wait." It does not say for what. The faction's candidate will be crowned in three years.

choices.text: Bring the order before the Court

effects.log: The Court reads it and falls into an argument about grammar that lasts the whole three years. The crowning is postponed. (+30 fame)

choices.text: Burn it: the Court has waited enough

effects.log: The ash is very light. You never tell anyone. The crowning goes ahead. (-5 align, +4 merit)

choices.text: Keep it, and say nothing yet

effects.log: You keep the order in your sleeve. It weighs more than paper should. (+2 luck)

events.text: On the morning the crowning should have happened, the throne is not empty. Someone is sitting in it: a figure of light, too bright to look at, who seems to have been there all along. The whole Court kneels. The figure looks, very briefly, at you.

effects.log: You kneel. The light passes over you like a warm hand. When it is gone, so is the figure, and every minister walks out looking younger. (+100 years of life)
You stand. For a breath you understand what the throne was waiting for, and then you do not. The Court will talk about you for a thousand years. (+5 Mind, +60 fame)

choices.text: Ask it what it waited for

effects.log: It answers, but in a voice made of weather. Afterwards the clouds over the Court are gentler for a hundred years, and nobody can say why. (+6 align)

events.text: The candidate is crowned. For a hundred years the Court is very orderly and nobody laughs in the corridors. Then the new sovereign summons you, alone, and asks whether the throne ever spoke to anyone before.

choices.text: Tell the truth about the order that said wait

effects.log: The sovereign is quiet a long time, then sets the crown on the empty throne's arm and walks out. The Court has two thrones now, and argues about which to bow to. (+6 align)
The sovereign seems relieved, and raises you high. You sleep badly for a decade. (+8 merit)

events.text: A province below has had no rain for three years. You look into it and find the reason in a ledger: a rain official of the Court was insulted there two hundred years ago by a drunk at a festival, and has been withholding rain ever since, very precisely, from that one province.

effects.log: The official is charming, sorry, and entirely unwilling. "The insult is still standing," the official says. "So am I." (+2 Mind)
You send one rain, at night. In the morning the province dances, and the official knows exactly who did it. (+5 align)

choices.text: Leave it: it is not your ministry

effects.log: You close the ledger. The drought goes into its fourth year. (+2 merit)

events.text: The rain official files a complaint against you with the Court: interference in a ministry. The hearing is in a hall full of clouds, all of them waiting to see which way to blow. The drought below is in its fourth year.

choices.text: Argue that the insult died with the drunk

ok.log: "The man is two hundred years in his grave," you say. "Your grudge has outlived its reason." The Court agrees. The rain falls for a month. (+5 merit, +5 align)

fail.log: The Court rules that an insult is an insult. The drought goes on. You are fined in merit. (-3 merit)

choices.text: Find the drunk's descendant and bring an apology up the stairs

effects.log: It takes a year. The descendant is a nervous farmer who bows so low the official laughs, and forgives, and rains. (+6 align, +2 charm)

choices.text: Apologise yourself, on the province's behalf

effects.log: You bow to the official. The official, astonished, bows back. The rain comes the next morning. (+4 align)

events.text: Years later the rain official comes to your door with a jar of rainwater from the province: the first rain, kept. "I had forgotten," the official says, "what it looks like from below. They hold their hands out."

effects.log: It tastes of dust and green things. You sit until dusk without needing to say much. (+3 charm, +100 years of life)

choices.text: Pour it back down to the province

effects.log: It falls as a single warm shower on one field. A farmer stands in it laughing. (+5 align, +2 luck)

events.text: You are seated on a Celestial Tribunal. The accused is a young immortal who went down the white stairs without leave and spent forty years as a village doctor below. Descent is forbidden. The village is begging, in a thousand prayers, for the doctor to be sent back.

effects.log: You vote to pardon. You are outvoted, but your name is on the dissent, and the dissent is read in every ministry. (+5 align, +20 fame)

choices.text: Vote to punish, as the law says

effects.log: The law is the law. The doctor is confined to a cloud for a thousand years. You rise in the Court's esteem. (+5 merit)

choices.text: Ask to hear the doctor first

effects.log: The doctor speaks for an hour about a child's fever and a broken well. Half the tribunal looks at the floor. (+3 Mind)

events.text: A message reaches you from the cloud of confinement: the young doctor has found a way to see the village from there, and the village is sick again. A fever. The doctor asks nothing; the message only says what the fever is, and what would cure it.

choices.text: Go down yourself and cure it

effects.log: You break the same law in the same place. The fever breaks. The Court, very carefully, does not notice. (+8 align, -4 merit)

choices.text: Send the cure down on the wind

effects.log: Seeds of a herb fall on the village and grow in a night. Nobody below knows why. (+5 align)

choices.text: Petition the Court to send the doctor back

effects.log: The petition takes a decade. The fever does not wait for it. You learn something about the Court that you did not want to. (+2 merit, -2 align)

events.text: The village below has built a shrine. On it, side by side, are two carved figures: the doctor, and someone who looks a great deal like you. The Court has seen it. A minister asks whether you would like the shrine removed.

effects.log: It stands. Mortals bring it bowls of rice. Up here, some young immortals start to visit the stairs at night. (+30 fame, +4 align)

choices.text: Ask for the doctor's pardon in exchange for the shrine

effects.log: The minister considers, and agrees. The doctor walks free and the shrine is gone by morning; the village keeps a carving in a cupboard. (+6 align)

events.text: The Jade Void Sect stands on two floating peaks joined by one bridge, and the peaks have not spoken to each other for six thousand years over a sword form neither will name. This year the Western Peak's head challenges the Eastern Peak's head to a duel on the bridge. Both ask you to be their second.

effects.log: You stand on the west end of the bridge. The east end looks at you the way a cliff looks at weather. (+3 merit)
You stand on the east end. The west end sends a polite note to say it will remember. (+3 merit)

choices.text: Ask what the quarrel is about

effects.log: Nobody remembers. Both heads are quietly embarrassed you asked. (+3 Mind)

events.text: On the morning of the duel, you find out what the quarrel was about: a library scroll. Six thousand years ago someone borrowed the second half of a sword form from the Eastern Peak and never brought it back. The scroll is under a loose stone of the bridge, where the borrower hid it and then forgot.

choices.text: Lay it on the bridge between them

effects.log: The two heads read it together, then look at each other, then laugh until the bridge shakes. The duel becomes a lesson. (+6 align, +30 fame)
It is the most beautiful sword form you have ever seen, and it is only half. You keep the other half in your head. (+5 Mind)

choices.text: Let the duel happen and keep the scroll for later

roll.foeName: a sword immortal of the Jade Void

ok.log: You hold the duel to first blood and it is over in a heartbeat, both heads bowing. Nobody guesses you knew all along. (+5 merit)

fail.log: The duel goes wrong, as duels between old masters do. You step between the blades and pay for it. (-15 health)

events.text: The Jade Void's two peaks have drifted a little closer since the bridge. The sect elders want to name the whole form after the one who found it. They come to you with a brush.

choices.text: Let them name it after you

effects.log: The form is taught under your name. Ten thousand years from now, someone will think you invented it. (+50 fame, +4 merit)

choices.text: Name it after the borrower who forgot

effects.log: The form is called the Forgotten Half. The sect laughs at itself for the first time in six thousand years. (+5 charm, +4 align)

events.text: Beneath the Jade Void's mountain is the Sword Tomb, where the swords of dead immortals hang point down in the dark, ten thousand of them, waiting for a hand worthy of them. Elders go down once in a century to see if any will move. This century they take you. One sword moves.

effects.log: It comes to your hand like a bird. The elders are silent all the way back up. (+4 merit, +2 Mind)

choices.text: Bow to it and leave it

effects.log: You bow, and the sword settles. The elders look at you strangely: nobody has ever refused one. (+5 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Ask the elders whose it was

effects.log: There is a long silence. "A traitor's," one says at last. "Executed nine thousand years ago." The sword trembles. (+3 Mind)

events.text: The sword that chose you belonged, the records say, to an immortal executed for treason. But at night the sword shows you its memories, and in them its owner was not a traitor: an elder of the time wanted the owner's place, and wrote the charge.

choices.text: Bring the memories before the sect

effects.log: The elders sit through the memories in silence. The executed immortal is cleared, nine thousand years late. A portrait goes back up. (+8 align, +30 fame)

choices.text: Keep the sword and the secret

effects.log: You carry it, and say nothing. The sword is quieter in your hand than any blade you have held. (+2 luck)
The accuser's heir is a Grand Elder now, who knows exactly what you have found. (+3 Mind)

events.text: The Grand Elder whose ancestor wrote the false charge comes to see you, alone, without a sword. "I knew," the Grand Elder says. "I have always known. I am asking you to let it lie."

choices.text: Let it lie, for the price of the Grand Elder's seat in a century

effects.log: The Grand Elder nods, slowly. A century later the seat is empty and your name is on it. (+10 merit, -6 align)

choices.text: Refuse, and bring the truth out

effects.log: The truth comes out. The Grand Elder resigns with more dignity than the ancestor had. (+8 align, +3 merit)

choices.text: Duel for it, as the sect's law allows

roll.foeName: the Grand Elder of the Jade Void

ok.log: You win, cleanly. The Grand Elder kneels and tells the truth to the whole sect. (+6 merit, +40 fame)

fail.log: You lose, and by the sect's law, the matter is closed. The sword hums in its sheath for a year, angry for you. (-12 health)

events.text: A junior immortal of the Jade Void, practising alone at dawn, gets a cut slightly too right and takes a slice off the corner of the floating mountain. The mountain tips by a hair. Every teacup in the sect slides an inch. The elders want an example made.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Cut the Mountain

effects.log: "They cut a mountain," you say. "Teach them to aim." The elders grumble and give the junior to you. (+3 align)
The junior is sent to guard the bridge for a century. The mountain is levelled with weights. (+3 merit)

choices.text: Go and look at the cut

effects.log: It is the cleanest edge you have ever seen. You stand there for an hour. (+3 Mind)

events.text: The junior trains under your eye for years and is terrifying: one cut in every hundred is a cut that should not be possible. Then the Demon Realm hears of it and sends an envoy with an offer the junior has not yet refused.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Cut the Mountain

choices.text: Tell the junior to choose freely

effects.log: The junior thinks for a month and stays. "You did not tell me what to do," the junior says. "Nobody here ever does that." (+5 align, +4 merit)

ok.log: The envoy goes home with a story about the Jade Void that frightens the Demon Realm for a century. (+5 merit, +20 fame)

fail.log: The envoy goes home bruised but laughing, and the offer stays open. (-10 health)

choices.text: Let the junior go, and wish them well

effects.log: The junior goes down to the Demon Realm, and writes to you for a while, and then stops. (+2 charm)

events.text: The junior, now an elder of the Jade Void, takes a slice off a stray storm that was drifting toward the sect, cleanly, and the storm falls apart into rain. Everybody turns to look at you, as if you had done it.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Cut the Mountain

choices.text: Point at the one who did it

effects.log: The sect cheers the new elder. Afterwards the new elder brings you tea and does not say thank you, which is how you know. (+4 align, +3 merit)

choices.text: Take a bow, as a joke

effects.log: The new elder laughs harder than anyone has ever seen. The sect never quite knows who cut the storm. (+3 charm, +20 fame)

events.text: The Jade Void's founding ancestor went into seclusion thirty thousand years ago, and every year the sect leaves food at the sealed door, and every year the food is gone. This year a rumour runs through the halls: the ancestor is long dead, and certain elders eat the food to keep the sect obedient.

effects.log: At midnight the food is taken by a crane. Just a crane. You do not know whether that is better or worse. (+3 Mind)
You speak against it in the hall. The rumour goes quiet, and so do certain elders, who look at you gratefully. (+4 merit)
You knock. Nothing. Then, very faintly, a knock comes back. (+2 luck)

events.text: You follow the crane. It flies to a crack in the mountain's underside and in, and you squeeze in after it, and find the ancestor: not dead, not alive, sitting in a lotus of stone, having become, slowly, part of the mountain. The crane lays the food in the ancestor's lap. The ancestor's eyes open.

effects.log: "Nothing," the ancestor says, in a voice like rock settling. "I am holding the mountain up. Tell them to stop worrying." (+5 Mind)
The ancestor teaches you one thing, which takes eleven years, and is how to stand still. (+5 Mind, +100 years of life)
You back out of the crack. The crane watches you go. You will not say what you saw. (+2 align)

events.text: You tell the sect what the ancestor is doing. Half the elders are moved. The other half are alarmed: if the ancestor is the mountain, then whoever the ancestor favours could command it. They look at you.

effects.log: "I asked for nothing," you say, "and nothing was given." The alarmed half relax, mostly. (+4 align, +3 merit)

choices.text: Say the ancestor asked for you to be heard

effects.log: It is not quite true and it is very effective. The elders seat you higher. (+8 merit, -4 align)

choices.text: Bring the elders to the ancestor

effects.log: They come, and kneel, and the ancestor says one sentence to each, and none of them will ever repeat theirs. (+30 fame, +3 merit)

events.text: A Demon General you fought on the border used a Jade Void sword form, the secret one, the one taught only to elders. Somebody sold it. The Jade Void would rather not know who. You would.
events.arc: The Elder Who Sold the Sword

effects.log: You start keeping a list of elders who have new things they cannot explain. It is a short list. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Raise it in the elders' hall

effects.log: The hall goes very quiet. Somebody in it is now afraid of you. (+3 merit)
Forms leak. Sects survive. You put it out of your mind, almost. (+2 luck)

events.text: The list narrows to one elder: kind, beloved, the teacher of half the sect's young immortals. The elder sold the form to buy back a disciple held hostage in the Demon Realm, and has paid for it every night since.
events.arc: The Elder Who Sold the Sword

effects.log: You keep it. The elder knows you know, and teaches better than ever, as if to pay. (+4 align)
The elder confesses before you can speak. The sect is merciful, as far as sects go: a century on the bridge. (+5 merit)

choices.text: Go and fetch back what was sold

effects.log: You go to the Demon General and win the form back the hard way. (+4 merit, -10 health)

events.text: The disciple the old elder ransomed comes to you, grown, an elder too now, and lays a sword at your feet. "I know what it cost," the disciple says, "and who kept quiet. Whatever you need, for as long as I live."
events.arc: The Elder Who Sold the Sword

choices.text: Ask only that it be passed on

effects.log: "Do the same for someone else," you say. The disciple does, many times. (+5 align, +3 merit)
The oath is sworn on the Jade Void bridge. You have an ally for ten thousand years. (+5 merit, +20 fame)

events.text: The Nine Clouds Palace is making a pill that takes nine hundred years: one century on each of the nine clouds, each palace adding its turn. The seventh turn falls to you. The pill arrives in a cauldron the size of a pavilion, humming, and with it a note from the sixth palace: "Do not let the third palace near it."

choices.text: Bar the third palace from your cloud

effects.log: The third palace is insulted and says so in verse. The pill hums on undisturbed. (+3 merit)

choices.text: Invite the third palace to watch

effects.log: They come, curious, and are so charmed to be trusted that they bring their own best fire. (+3 charm)
The sixth palace will only say "the second turn". You go and read the records of the second turn. (+3 Mind)

events.text: Seventy years into your century, the pill's colour goes wrong: a thread of grey in the gold. Somebody has slipped a seed of decay into it. If you report it, the pill is lost and nine hundred years with it. If you can draw the seed out, nobody need ever know.

ok.log: It takes you a year of never sleeping. The seed comes out like a splinter. The gold is whole again, and nobody ever knows. (+5 Mind, +4 merit)

fail.log: The seed breaks as you draw it. The pill is saved, but smaller, and the palace will notice. (-3 merit, -8 health)

effects.log: The palace masters convene. The pill is not lost after all: the masters draw the seed out together, and look at one another very hard. (+4 merit)

choices.text: Find who put it there first

effects.log: The seed carries a faint scent. You know that scent: the sixth palace's incense. (+3 Mind)

events.text: You confront the sixth palace's master with the scent. The master admits it at once, without shame: the pill, finished, would raise one palace above the other eight forever, and the sixth palace is not the one it was made for.

choices.text: Keep their secret, for a share of the pill

effects.log: You keep it. When the pill is finished a sliver of it comes to you in a plain box. (+150 years of life, -6 align)

choices.text: Expose them before all nine palaces

effects.log: The sixth palace is cast down a cloud. The pill is finished in peace and you are thanked very loudly. (+8 merit)

choices.text: Ask the nine palaces to share the pill instead

effects.log: It takes a century of argument. In the end the pill is cut in nine, and nobody rises above anyone, and everybody is a little stronger. (+6 align, +40 fame)

events.text: Nine hundred years end on a single morning. The pill is finished, and the whole palace gathers on the ninth cloud to see it opened. It glows. It is, quite clearly, the greatest pill made in ten thousand years. The Palace Lord turns and offers you the honour of the first taste.

effects.log: It tastes of every century it was made in. You feel nine hundred years of other immortals' patience settle in your bones. (+300 years of life)

choices.text: Give the taste to the oldest master present

effects.log: The oldest master cries, which nobody in the palace has ever seen. You are not forgotten. (+6 align, +5 merit)

events.text: The great furnace of the Nine Clouds Palace has burned since before the sun was lit. This year, tending it, you hear it speak. It says, in a voice like coals shifting, that it is tired of pills. It would like, just once, to make something for itself.

choices.text: Ask it what it would make

effects.log: "A bird," says the furnace, "of fire, that flies away." You promise to think about it. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Report it to the palace masters

effects.log: The masters come and listen and hear nothing; the furnace is silent for them. They look at you with concern. (+1 merit)

choices.text: Feed it its favourite fuel and say nothing

effects.log: You find that it likes peach wood best. It burns for you more sweetly than for anyone. (+2 luck, +2 merit)

events.text: You and the furnace work out the bird together, at night, between pills: a little flame-thing with wings, more spirit than fire. It will take the furnace's own heart-ember to make it. If the furnace gives that, it will go out for a hundred years. The palace would lose a century.

effects.log: The bird flies out of the furnace mouth at dawn and circles the ninth cloud singing. The furnace goes dark and content. The palace is in uproar. (+8 align, -6 merit)
"Not yet," you say. The furnace burns lower for a year, sulking, and then forgives you. (+3 merit)

choices.text: Find a way to make the bird without the heart-ember

ok.log: You lend it a sliver of your own qi instead. The bird is small and fierce, the furnace stays lit, and you sleep for a month. (+6 Mind, +4 align)

fail.log: The bird comes out as a puff of smoke shaped like a sparrow, and drifts away. The furnace laughs, which is alarming. (+2 charm)

events.text: The fire-bird has made its nest on the Nine Clouds' highest roof. Pills baked under it come out finer than any in the palace's records. The masters, who were furious, have begun pretending it was their idea.

effects.log: You say nothing. The furnace knows. The bird knows. That is enough. (+4 align, +3 merit)

choices.text: Tell the true story in the palace annals

effects.log: It goes in the annals, in small characters, near the end. A thousand years from now a young alchemist will read it and listen to the furnace. (+30 fame, +3 Mind)

events.text: The Palace Lord of Nine Clouds is stepping down after eight thousand years, and the nine palaces will choose a new one by vote. Votes, up here, are bought with pills. Three palace masters send you a box each. Each box is heavier than the one before.

effects.log: The boxes come back to their senders. Two are offended. One is impressed and asks your opinion of the candidates. (+4 align)
A pill that takes a hundred years off the next breakthrough, and a note naming the price: your voice. (+100 years of life, -4 align)
There is a silence across nine clouds. Then a little laughter. Then, from two palaces, no laughter at all. (+20 fame)

events.text: The vote is a year off and the palace is a nest of whispers. One candidate is brilliant and cruel. One is kind and ordinary. One is ancient and asleep most days. Everyone knows your voice can tip it.

effects.log: The brilliant one wins, and the palace makes better pills than ever and is unhappier than ever. (+6 merit)
The kind one wins by your voice. The pills are not the best in the Upper Realm. The palace sings again in the evenings. (+5 align, +3 merit)

choices.text: Back the sleeping one, so nobody rules

effects.log: The sleeping one wins. The nine palaces govern themselves for a thousand years and it goes surprisingly well. (+4 Mind, +3 merit)

events.text: The vote comes. To your astonishment, and that of the palace, you have a real following: the young stewards, mostly, and the furnace-tenders, who have never had anyone to vote for before.

choices.text: Make your case on the ninth cloud

ok.log: You speak, and the young stewards cheer, and the old masters do sums. You come third, which up here is a beginning. (+40 fame, +6 merit)

fail.log: You speak too long. The old masters fall asleep, then the young ones. You come last, honourably. (+2 Mind)

choices.text: Withdraw and give your votes to the kind one

effects.log: The kind one wins by your votes, and makes you steward of the furnaces, which you find you like. (+5 align, +5 merit)

events.text: A pill recipe has been stolen from the Nine Clouds vault: the one for a pill that lets an immortal forget a single memory. A young cloud steward has been arrested for it. The steward is shaking, and was, you happen to know, with you the night of the theft.

effects.log: You say where the steward was. The masters frown and let the steward go, and now somebody else is looking for a thief. (+5 align)
You keep out of it. The steward is sent to the lowest cloud. You wonder, at night, why you were so careful. (-4 align, +2 merit)
You start with the vault, and the vault's keeper, who is far too calm. (+3 Mind)

events.text: The thief is a palace master, old and famous, who wanted the pill for one purpose only: to forget the face of a disciple who died in the master's care, ten thousand years ago. The master has made the pill. It is in a cup on the table between you.

effects.log: The master drinks. Afterwards the master is lighter and stranger and cannot remember why there is an empty chair in the study. (+3 align)
"Keep the face," you say. "It is the last of them." The master weeps and thanks you and resents you a little. (+4 Mind, +2 merit)
You forget one thing. You do not know what. Sometimes you reach for it in the night. (+4 Mind, -2 luck)

events.text: The old palace master sends for you. On the table is the face, at last: a portrait, painted from memory over a century, of the disciple who died. "I kept it," the master says, "because you would not let me throw it away. Now I can hang it."

choices.text: Help hang it in the palace hall

effects.log: The portrait goes up in the Nine Clouds hall. Young alchemists ask whose it is, and the master tells them, every time. (+5 align, +3 merit)

choices.text: Ask to hear about the disciple

effects.log: The master talks until the stars come out. You learn three recipes nobody has written down. (+5 Mind)

events.text: The seventh cloud of the Nine Clouds Palace is sinking again, a span every year, and the array that holds it up is missing stones. Somebody is prising them out, one a night, and the stones are worth a kingdom each in the world below.

choices.text: Set a watch on the array

effects.log: You sit up nine nights. On the ninth a shadow comes, takes a stone, and leaves a pill in its place, as if paying. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Replace the stones from your own store

effects.log: It costs you dearly. The cloud stops sinking. The palace thanks you and does not ask where you found them. (+5 merit, -20 qi)

choices.text: Redraw the array so it needs fewer stones

ok.log: You redraw it with half the stones. The cloud rises a little. The masters copy your lines onto every cloud. (+6 merit, +3 Mind)

fail.log: Your new array holds, but hums a note that keeps the whole palace awake for a year. (+1 merit)

events.text: You follow the stone-thief down through the clouds, all the way to the white stairs, and watch it climb down them: an immortal, carrying the stones to a mortal kingdom below, where a famine has lasted seven years. The stones are being sold for grain.

effects.log: You go home and say nothing. The famine below breaks in a year. The seventh cloud sinks another span. (+8 align, -3 merit)

choices.text: Stop the immortal on the stairs

effects.log: You stop the thief on the stairs. The thief does not fight, only asks you to look down. You look. (+3 merit)

choices.text: Offer to carry grain down yourself, openly

effects.log: You petition the palace to feed the kingdom. They think it beneath them, and then they think of how it will sound in the annals. (+6 align, +20 fame)

events.text: The thief from the stairs is brought before the palace masters. They want to know who taught the thief the array well enough to unpick it. The thief looks at you, and does not say your name.

effects.log: You take your share of the blame. The masters fine you both, and quietly send grain down the stairs. (+5 align, -3 merit)
The thief is cast down a cloud. You keep your rank, and a stone in your chest. (+3 merit, -5 align)

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion reads a prophecy in the deep stars and finds, written across a whole constellation, your name. It is the most valuable thing the Pavilion has read in a thousand years. The Pavilion Master would like to sell it: to you, at a price, or to whoever pays more.

effects.log: It costs you a century of service and every favour you hold. The prophecy is one line. You read it alone. (+5 Mind, -6 merit)

choices.text: Refuse to buy your own fate

effects.log: You refuse. The Master shrugs: there are other buyers. You feel, for a while, watched from far off. (+3 align)

ok.log: You lie on the Pavilion roof for a year and read until your eyes ache with light. You get all of it. (+5 Mind)

fail.log: You lie on the roof a year and get half of it, and a headache that lasts a decade. (+2 Mind, -6 health)

events.text: The prophecy says you will, at some unspecified time, stand at the edge of the heavens and decide whether they go on. It does not say what you decide. In smaller stars it says that someone close to you will try to make the decision for you.

effects.log: You tell no one, and from then on watch everyone, which is tiring. (+2 luck)
The Master listens kindly, and quietly sells the second half to someone else. You find out a year later. (+2 Mind, -2 merit)
You burn it. The constellation in the sky stays exactly where it was. (+3 Mind)

events.text: A stranger finds you on a drifting isle: an immortal with the Star Sea's seal, carrying a copy of your prophecy, bought at a great price. "I came to see," the stranger says, "what kind of person they think is going to decide whether the heavens go on."

effects.log: The stranger looks for a long time and then laughs, and sits down, and shares a gourd of cloud wine. You are friends by dusk. (+4 charm)

choices.text: Take the copy back by force

ok.log: The stranger yields the copy and goes, chastened. The Star Sea, hearing, raises its prices for you. (+3 merit)

fail.log: The stranger is stronger than they looked, and leaves with the copy and your dignity. (-12 health)

effects.log: The stranger thinks about it seriously, which you did not expect. "Go on," they say. "Always go on." (+4 Mind, +3 align)

events.text: Three of the stars the Star Sea Pavilion reads by have begun to lie. Readings come out wrong: a war foretold that never comes, a sage's death that does not happen. You trace the lies to one star, small and bright, that was not on any chart a thousand years ago.

effects.log: You watch it a whole year. It moves, very slightly, when a reader looks at it. It is listening. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Report it to the Pavilion Master

effects.log: The Master goes pale, then very calm, and tells you to say nothing to the other readers. (+3 merit)

choices.text: Read by the old stars only

effects.log: Your readings come out true and slow and the buyers grumble. (+2 luck)

events.text: The new star is not a star. It is an artefact: a mirror hung in the sky by somebody who wanted the Star Sea Pavilion's readings bent, slightly, in one direction. Every lie it told favoured the Demon Realm.

effects.log: You fly to it and take it down, and it is the size of a teacup and very cold. (+5 merit, +20 fame)
You turn it a hair. Now it lies for the Pavilion. Nobody ever finds out. (+6 merit, -6 align)

choices.text: Leave it, and read the lies backwards

effects.log: Lies have a shape. For a decade you read the Demon Realm's wishes in the stars. (+5 Mind)

events.text: The Pavilion keeps the sky-mirror in its vault. One night it shows you, in its cold face, who hung it: a former Star Elder, cast out long ago, still in the Pavilion's oldest robes, living in the Demon Realm, very lonely.

choices.text: Go and find the old elder

effects.log: You find a tired immortal in a borrowed tower who only wanted to be listened to again. You listen. (+5 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Report the name to the Pavilion

effects.log: The Pavilion sends assassins of a very polite kind. You do not ask how it ends. (+5 merit, -3 align)

events.text: A mortal emperor from the world below has sent a ladder of gold up the white stairs, and an envoy up the ladder, to buy a reading from the Star Sea Pavilion: the hour and manner of the dynasty's end. The Pavilion gives the reading to you.

effects.log: The dynasty ends in two hundred years, in a peasant rebellion, without much blood. You write it down plainly. (+3 merit)
You write that the dynasty will end "when heaven wills", which is true and useless. The envoy is delighted. (+2 merit, -2 align)

choices.text: Refuse to read a mortal kingdom's death

effects.log: The Pavilion fines you, and sells the reading through somebody else. (+4 align, -3 merit)

events.text: The emperor, having read the truth, does something no emperor has done in your memory. The court below is cutting taxes, opening granaries, sending officials to the villages to ask what the peasants want. The Pavilion's other readers are furious: a reading that changes the future is worth less next time.

effects.log: "The stars said what would happen if nothing changed," you say. "Something changed." The readers grumble and do not answer. (+5 align)
You read it again. It now ends in six hundred years, quietly, in a library. (+4 Mind, +20 fame)
You apologise. The readers forgive you. Below, the emperor goes on opening granaries anyway. (+3 merit)

events.text: Six hundred years pass. The dynasty below ends, in a library, as you read it would. Its last emperor sends one more envoy up the stairs, not to buy anything, but to bring the Star Sea Pavilion the dynasty's own history, finished, and a note for you.

effects.log: It says: "Thank you for telling us the truth. It gave us time." You keep it for a thousand years. (+5 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Give the history a place in the Pavilion

effects.log: It is the only mortal book in the Pavilion's vault. Readers start borrowing it. (+4 merit, +20 fame)

events.text: You notice it before anyone else: the Pavilion Master of the Star Sea can no longer see the stars. The Master's readings come out of a careful memory of skies ten thousand years old, and so far they have been right by luck. The Master knows you know.

choices.text: Offer to read for the Master, in secret

effects.log: For years your readings go out under the Master's seal. The Master pours your tea, very carefully, without seeing the cup. (+5 merit)

choices.text: Tell the Master it is time to step down

effects.log: The Master is silent a long time. "Not yet," the Master says. "Let me finish one more chart." (+3 align)
You keep your counsel. The readings go out, half memory, half luck. (+2 luck)

events.text: The Star Elders smell weakness. One of them, ambitious and brilliant, has guessed the Master's secret and means to expose it before the whole Pavilion at the Night of Long Reading, and take the Master's seat.

effects.log: The Master hears you out, then laughs softly. "Let the elder speak," the Master says. "I have one last reading left in me." (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Out-read the ambitious elder in public

ok.log: You read a sky so far out that the elder cannot follow. Nobody remembers the accusation afterwards, only the reading. (+30 fame, +6 merit)

fail.log: The elder reads better. The secret comes out. The Master steps down with grace, and the new Master does not forget you. (-4 merit)

effects.log: The secret comes out. The Master steps down. The elder takes the seat and is exactly as brilliant and unkind as you feared. (+2 merit)

events.text: On the Night of Long Reading the old Master stands at the Pavilion's edge, blind, and reads the sky aloud from memory: a sky of ten thousand years ago, every star in its old place. Then the Master says, "And this is how it has changed," and reads every change, from the sound of the readers' breathing.

choices.text: Lead the Pavilion in a bow

effects.log: The whole Pavilion bows. The ambitious elder bows lowest. The Master steps down that night, in glory. (+5 align, +4 merit)

choices.text: Ask the Master to teach you that

effects.log: It takes a century. Afterwards you can read the sky with your eyes shut, by the hush it makes. (+6 Mind)

events.text: Two Star Readers of the Pavilion have read the same sky and come out with opposite answers: one says the Celestial Ministries and the Demon Realm will go to war within the century, the other that they will make peace. Both readings have been sold, to different buyers. One of them must be wrong, and the Pavilion's name with it.

effects.log: You read for a month. Both are right: the sky is undecided. Something has not happened yet. (+4 Mind)
The war reader is grateful and loud about it. The peace reader stops greeting you. (+3 merit)
The peace reader brings you plum cakes for a decade. The war reader writes you into a lesser chart. (+3 align)

events.text: You find the thing that has not happened yet: a meeting, a hundred years off, between a marshal of the Court and a duke of the Demon Realm, at a tea pavilion on a drifting isle. Whatever is said there decides the sky.

effects.log: You arrange for the tea pavilion to be open, the tea to be good, and the isle to drift in the right direction. (+5 align)

choices.text: Sell the time and place to the Court

effects.log: The Court pays handsomely. The marshal goes to the meeting with a hidden army. (+8 merit, -6 align)
You close your charts. Some things should not be read too closely. (+3 Mind)

events.text: A hundred years later, at a tea pavilion on a drifting isle, a marshal and a duke sit down, and you are pouring the tea. The marshal is proud. The duke is tired. Neither wants to speak first.

ok.log: You say, "The tea is getting cold." They both laugh. By the third pot they are arguing about borders, not wars. The sky decides for peace. (+8 align, +50 fame)

fail.log: Your first word is the wrong one. They leave cold and polite. The sky, for now, stays undecided. (+2 Mind)

effects.log: You pour for an hour. At last the duke says, "Your tea is very good," and something begins. (+5 align, +3 charm)

events.text: In the Demon Realm you hold a fortress of black glass on the border of the clouds. A Demon Duke covets it, and in the Demon Realm coveting is a formal process: a herald arrives with a challenge written on a sheet of beaten iron. One month.
events.arc: The Duke Who Wanted Your Fortress

effects.log: You nail the iron sheet over your gate. The whole border comes to watch the month go by. (+3 merit)

choices.text: Offer the Duke half the fortress

effects.log: The Duke is so puzzled by the offer that the challenge is withdrawn for further study. (+2 Mind)
You walk out with what you can carry. The Demon Realm thinks less of you, and the Duke thinks more. (-4 merit, +3 align)

events.text: The month is up. The Duke arrives at your black gate with a mountain-sized war-beast, two hundred retainers and a band. The fight, by Demon Realm custom, is yours alone.
events.arc: The Duke Who Wanted Your Fortress

ok.log: You win. The Duke kneels, laughing, and swears to you on the spot, because that is also custom. (+10 merit, +40 fame)

fail.log: You lose, and by custom keep your life but not your fortress. The Duke sends you a fruit basket. (-20 health, -4 merit)

choices.text: Fight the war-beast instead, and befriend it

effects.log: The war-beast was never asked anything in its life. It sits down. The Duke, without a mount, goes home. (+5 align, +4 merit)
You yield. The Duke takes the fortress and, oddly, keeps your banner flying under the new one. (+2 charm, -3 merit)

events.text: The Duke you beat now serves you, after a fashion: loudly, faithfully and with frequent challenges to your other retainers. Then the Duke comes to you quietly with news. The Demon Emperor has heard about the fortress, and wants it too.
events.arc: The Duke Who Wanted Your Fortress

choices.text: Send the Duke to the Emperor with your respects

effects.log: The Duke comes back alive, which is the Emperor's way of saying it will wait. (+5 merit)

choices.text: Ready the fortress for a siege

effects.log: The border holds its breath for a year. The Emperor's army never comes; the Emperor was only seeing who would flinch. (+4 merit, +3 luck)

events.text: You and the Duke now share the black fortress, one wing each, and are the most confusing household on the border. Retainers do not know whom to bow to. The Duke proposes a feast to settle it.
events.arc: The Duke Who Wanted Your Fortress

effects.log: The feast lasts nine days and ends with both of your banners sewn into one. (+5 charm, +3 merit)

choices.text: Settle it with a game of go

effects.log: You win the game; the Duke wins the rematch; you decide not to play a third. The household is very relieved. (+4 Mind)

events.text: Your demon captains have caught a Celestial Officer of the Celestial Ministries spying on the border and hung the officer in a cage of thorns above your hall. They are waiting to see what you will do. In the Demon Realm, what you do with a captive is how everyone learns who you are.
events.arc: The Court Officer in the Cage

choices.text: Ransom the officer to the Court

effects.log: The Court pays in jade, and the officer goes home with an expression you will remember. (+5 merit)

choices.text: Let the officer go in the night

effects.log: You open the cage yourself. Your captains see. Nobody says anything. (+6 align, -3 merit)
You have the officer brought down and fed. You talk every evening for a year. (+4 Mind)

events.text: A message comes from the Celestial Ministries, through very discreet channels. The officer you dealt kindly with has risen to Star Marshal, and has not forgotten. The Marshal offers a secret line between the Court and you: no treason, only a way to warn each other when something truly terrible comes.
events.arc: The Court Officer in the Cage

effects.log: A cloud-sparrow comes to your window once a decade after that, with nothing much to say. You find you look forward to it. (+5 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Refuse: the Demon Realm would call it treason

effects.log: You refuse. The Marshal understands. Your captains, who hear of it, trust you more. (+5 merit)

events.text: The cloud-sparrow comes out of season, frantic. Something is crossing the deep sky toward both the Court and the Demon Realm: a swarm of void-moths that eat qi. The Marshal will hold the eastern clouds. Will you hold the west?
events.arc: The Court Officer in the Cage

ok.log: You hold it. The moths break on your border like spray. Afterwards nobody in either realm will say who stood together, and everybody knows. (+8 merit, +60 fame)

fail.log: You hold it, barely, and the Marshal holds it for you at the end. (-20 health, +4 merit)

choices.text: Warn the Demon Emperor and let the armies deal with it

effects.log: The armies deal with it, slowly, at great cost. The sparrow never comes again. (+3 merit, -3 align)

events.text: One of your demon captains, ferocious, horned and fiercely loyal, asks to speak to you alone. Before the captain went up to the Demon Realm, thirty thousand years ago, the captain was a fisher on a lake below. The captain wants to know if it is possible to go back down, and be small again.
events.arc: The Demon Who Wanted to Go Home

effects.log: You start asking. Nobody in the Demon Realm has ever asked that question before, and the question travels. (+4 align)

choices.text: Say the Demon Realm does not give back

effects.log: The captain bows and goes back to work, and is a little less ferocious ever after. (+3 merit)
The captain laughs with you, too loudly, and never asks again. (-3 align, +2 merit)

events.text: You have found the way: an old path down from the Demon Realm, not by the white stairs but by a waterfall, which washes off whatever a demon has become. It also washes off every year the demon has lived. The captain would arrive below young, remembering nothing.
events.arc: The Demon Who Wanted to Go Home

effects.log: The captain listens and is quiet for a month, then comes to you and says, "Yes." (+5 align)
You tell the captain only that it is possible. The captain begins to pack. (-3 align)
The captain believes you. You are not sure, afterwards, that you did the captain a kindness. (+2 merit)

events.text: At the top of the waterfall the captain takes off a war-crown worn for thirty thousand years and hands it to you. Below, very far down, there is a lake, and a reed boat on it.
events.arc: The Demon Who Wanted to Go Home

choices.text: Walk the captain to the edge

effects.log: The captain steps into the water and is gone, and far below a small figure climbs into the reed boat and looks around, puzzled and happy. (+8 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Ask the captain to stay one more year

effects.log: The captain stays a year, and you talk about fish. Then the captain goes, and you keep the crown on a shelf. (+4 charm, +4 align)

events.text: Three Demon Kings invite you to a dinner lit by black lanterns. Over the second course they explain that the Demon Emperor has grown old and cautious, and that on a certain night the lanterns of the palace will all go out at once. They would like you to be on their side when it happens. They do not say what the other side gets.

effects.log: You raise a cup of black wine. The three Kings smile with all their teeth. (+5 merit, -5 align)
You refuse. The Kings let you leave, which means they are sure you will not talk. (+2 Mind)
You go straight to the palace. The Emperor already knows. The Emperor wants to know why you came. (+6 merit)

events.text: The night of the black lanterns comes. Every lantern in the palace goes out. In the dark, swords; in the dark, the old Emperor laughing; in the dark, somebody running toward you.

ok.log: The palace is taken by morning. The old Emperor is gone, nobody says where. The new order gives you a crown of your own. (+12 merit, -6 align)

fail.log: The Emperor's guard was waiting. You fight your way out of the palace and do not stop until the border. (-25 health, -6 merit)

effects.log: You light a lantern and stand by the Emperor. The Kings see it and lose their nerve. The coup is over in an hour. (+8 merit, +3 align)
You stand in a doorway till dawn. Whoever wins will remember that you did not choose. (+2 luck, -3 merit)

events.text: The old Demon Emperor sends for you after the night of the black lanterns. The three Kings are in chains. The Emperor is eating plums. "You told me," the Emperor says. "Nobody tells me anything. Sit. What do you want?"

choices.text: Ask mercy for the three Kings

effects.log: The Emperor spits a plum stone and grants it, and the Kings are sent to the Abyss's edge to guard it forever, which is nearly mercy. (+6 align, +4 merit)
The Emperor gives you one, with its debts and its ghosts. (+12 merit)
The Emperor stares, then laughs until the plums roll off the table. "Nothing," the Emperor says. "I will remember that you are dangerous." (+4 Mind, +30 fame)

events.text: The Demon Realm sends you across the cloud border with a red banner and three hundred demons to raid a Celestial Ministries granary of star-rice. It is the oldest kind of war up here: nobody is meant to die, and everybody is meant to be humiliated.

choices.text: Lead the raid by the book

effects.log: You take the granary at dawn, leave a receipt, and are home by noon. The Demon Realm loves the receipt. (+6 merit, +20 fame)
You take half. The granary keeper notices, and sends a quiet thank-you note across the border. (+4 align, +3 merit)
Your demons are disgusted. You tell them you are saving the granary for a better year. (-4 merit, +2 Mind)

events.text: The Court answers the raid with a raid of its own, as is proper: a troop of Celestial Officers on cloud-horses comes to steal your banner. They come at night, singing, which is also proper.

ok.log: You keep the banner and take their captain's horse. Both realms agree it was a very good raid. (+5 merit, +20 fame)

fail.log: They take the banner, and your hat. You will never live down the hat. (-8 health, -2 merit)

choices.text: Let them have it, and sing back

effects.log: You give up the banner and out-sing them. They leave it on the border post the next morning, with a ribbon. (+4 charm)

events.text: A century of raids and counter-raids later, the granary keeper of the Celestial Ministries and you are old friends who have never met. The keeper sends a message: there is a famine coming to the world below, and both realms' granaries could stop it.

choices.text: Meet the keeper on the border

effects.log: You meet at last, and between you send down enough star-rice to feed three provinces. Neither realm is told. (+8 align)

choices.text: Report the message to the Demon Realm

effects.log: The Demon Realm sees an opening for a much bigger raid. You are rewarded. The world below goes hungry. (+8 merit, -8 align)

events.text: In the drifting rubble at the edge of the Upper Realm there is a door into the Ruins of the First Heaven, the heaven that fell before this one rose, and this year it is open. Just inside, the first room is a library. Its shelves float. Its books are written in a script nobody living can read, and they are reading you back.
events.arc: The Library of the First Heaven

effects.log: You walk for a year between drifting shelves, and begin, very slowly, to understand one word. (+5 Mind)
You take one. Outside the door it turns to sand, all but one page. You keep the page. (+3 luck, +2 Mind)
You bow to the shelves and leave. The door closes softly behind you, as if relieved. (+4 align)

events.text: The word you learned is the First Heaven's word for "enough". With it, the library opens a room it had kept shut: the records of why the First Heaven fell. Its immortals wanted everything. The heaven gave it to them.
events.arc: The Library of the First Heaven

choices.text: Read the records to the end

effects.log: You read for three years. When you come out, you are calmer than you have ever been. (+6 Mind, +3 align)

choices.text: Copy them for the Celestial Ministries

effects.log: The Court receives your copies, and files them, and does nothing. (+20 fame, +2 Mind)
You burn it so that no one can learn how to want everything. Something in the ruins sighs. (+3 align, -2 luck)

events.text: On your way out of the Ruins, the library's last shelf drifts after you to the door, carrying a single volume bound in white bark. It is blank. It wants, you understand, to be the first book of this heaven's fall, if it comes, and it wants you to keep it.
events.arc: The Library of the First Heaven

effects.log: You carry it home and never write in it, and every few centuries you check that it is still blank. (+4 luck, +100 years of life)

choices.text: Write one line in it, and give it back

effects.log: You write: "Not yet." The shelf drifts back into the dark with it. (+4 align, +3 Mind)

events.text: Deep in the Ruins of the First Heaven, in a courtyard where the flagstones float a hand's width off the ground, someone is sweeping. A small, old person in robes of a cut nobody has worn for an age, who looks up and says, in perfect and very old language, "Oh. Are you the new heaven?"
events.arc: The Last Citizen of the First Heaven

effects.log: The sweeper nods, as if this was expected, and offers you tea that has been brewing since the fall. (+4 Mind)

choices.text: Ask how long they have been sweeping

effects.log: "Since," the sweeper says, and seems to think that is a whole answer. (+3 Mind)
You leave the sweeper to the courtyard. The sound of the broom follows you a long way. (+2 align)

events.text: The last citizen of the First Heaven is not an immortal, or not only: a gardener who stayed behind to keep one courtyard tidy when everything else fell. The gardener is very tired. The broom is almost worn through.
events.arc: The Last Citizen of the First Heaven

choices.text: Bring the gardener out of the Ruins

effects.log: Outside, in this heaven's light, the gardener stands for a long time with their eyes closed. Then asks where the brooms are kept. (+8 align, +30 fame)

choices.text: Make a new broom and stay a while

effects.log: You sweep together for a year. The courtyard is the cleanest place in two heavens. (+5 Mind, +4 align)

choices.text: Ask the gardener what the First Heaven was like

effects.log: The gardener tells you about its evenings. You never quite manage to stop thinking about them. (+6 Mind)

events.text: The gardener you brought out of the Ruins has made a garden on a drifting isle and is growing, from seeds kept in a sleeve since the fall, flowers no one alive has seen. Immortals come from every faction to look at them, quietly.
events.arc: The Last Citizen of the First Heaven

effects.log: You tend it a decade. The flowers smell of an evening in a heaven that ended. (+5 align, +150 years of life)
The gardener gives you one, wrapped in a leaf, and says only: "It wants to be somewhere it will be looked at." (+4 luck, +3 charm)

events.text: At the centre of the Ruins of the First Heaven stands a throne, broken clean in two, and between the halves the air is thick as honey. Whoever sits on it, the inscription says, will hold whatever is left of the First Heaven's law.
events.arc: The Broken Throne of the First Heaven

effects.log: The throne was not broken by an enemy. It was broken from the inside, by its own sitter. (+4 Mind)
You sit. Something enormous and very old notices you. You stand up again rather quickly. (+4 Mind, -8 health)
You leave it. Some seats are a question nobody should answer. (+3 align)

events.text: Ever since you sat on the broken throne, the First Heaven's law has been trying to speak through you: in the middle of a conversation you will say a word in a language that ended an age ago, and the clouds around you will go still.
events.arc: The Broken Throne of the First Heaven

effects.log: You let it speak, once, on a high isle. It says one thing, which is a law about mercy, and then it is quiet for good. (+6 align, +4 Mind)

choices.text: Silence it with your own will

ok.log: You hold it down for a decade, and it goes still. Your own will has never been clearer. (+6 Mind)

fail.log: It slips out in a court hearing and a minister faints. The law goes quiet, embarrassed. (+2 Mind)

events.text: You have found the inscription on the back of the broken throne, the one the sitter carved before breaking it: "I was asked to hold a heaven, and I could not, and I am sorry." Below it, in another hand: "We forgive you."
events.arc: The Broken Throne of the First Heaven

effects.log: You carve your name. You do not know what it means, only that it belongs there. (+5 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Copy it out for the Celestial Ministries

effects.log: The Court's ministers read it in silence, and for a century are a little kinder in their judgements. (+30 fame)

events.text: At the bottom of the Sea of Falling Stars, where stars go down to drown, the hearts they leave behind still beat. You have dived there for months. Today you find a heart the size of a pavilion, beating slowly, warm through the water, and inside it, very faintly, something is singing.
events.arc: The Heart of a Drowned Star

effects.log: You listen until you forget to breathe, which up here you no longer need to. (+5 Mind)
The shard glows in your hand like an ember that will never go out. The singing stops. (+4 luck, -4 align)
You swim away. The sea is full of things that were not meant to be found. (+2 align)

events.text: The star's song is a map. It sings where the star used to hang in the sky, and who used to look at it from below: a shepherd, ten thousand years ago, who named it and told it every night about the sheep.
events.arc: The Heart of a Drowned Star

effects.log: It takes a year. When you surface you can name every star that ever fell. (+6 Mind)

choices.text: Try to lift the heart back into the sky

effects.log: You strain for a month and lift it a single span. It is grateful. (+5 align, -10 health)

events.text: The star's heart rises, slowly, out of the Sea of Falling Stars, the way a bubble rises, and goes on rising through the clouds. That night there is a new star above the world below, exactly where a shepherd's star used to be.
events.arc: The Heart of a Drowned Star

choices.text: Look down to see who notices

effects.log: A shepherd on a hillside below, a girl with a crook, stops and looks up, and names it, and starts telling it about the sheep. (+8 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Go back to the Sea for the others

effects.log: You dive again. There are ten thousand hearts down there, and you have time. (+4 Mind, +40 fame)

events.text: The shard you cut from the star's heart has not stopped glowing. Neither has it stopped being cold to everything except you. At night it hums the start of a song, then stops, as if waiting for its other half.
events.arc: The Heart of a Drowned Star

choices.text: Return the shard to the Sea

effects.log: You dive and press it back. The heart closes round it and, for a moment, sings. (+6 align, +2 Mind)
You keep it. It keeps you warm in a cold realm, and you never quite sleep well. (+4 luck, +100 years of life)

events.text: You are not alone in the Sea of Falling Stars. Another immortal is diving the same wreck-fields, faster than you, cheerfully taking every star-heart you swim toward a heartbeat before you reach it. Today the other diver waves.

effects.log: The other diver swims over and offers to split the next one. (+3 charm)

ok.log: You get there first. The other diver laughs bubbles and bows. (+4 luck, +20 fame)

fail.log: The other diver gets there first and tucks it away with a wink. (+2 Mind)

effects.log: You leave that field to the other diver. The deep currents are quieter anyway. (+2 Mind)

events.text: Deep in the Sea of Falling Stars, the other diver is caught: a drowned star has rolled over in its sleep and pinned the diver against the floor. The diver signs to you to go, there is nothing to be done.

ok.log: You lift it a hand's width and the diver slips out. You surface together, gasping, and the diver will not let go of your sleeve for an hour. (+8 align)

fail.log: You lift it, and it settles back on your arm. The diver pulls you both free. You owe each other now. (-15 health, +5 align)

effects.log: You surface and bring back three immortals and a rope of starlight. The diver is freed by nightfall. (+4 align)

events.text: The diver from the Sea of Falling Stars comes to find you, years later, with a gift wrapped in seaweed: the brightest heart either of you ever saw, the one the diver was swimming toward when the star rolled over.

effects.log: It lights your home for a thousand years. (+5 luck, +100 years of life)

choices.text: Dive with the diver one more time instead

effects.log: You dive together and give the heart back to the sea, which seems the right thing to do with it. (+5 align, +4 charm)

events.text: Diving the Sea of Falling Stars, you find a street on the sea floor: a row of little houses, a well, lanterns lit in every window, and nobody home. A town that fell with its star, and has been waiting since, every lantern still burning.

effects.log: Every door is unlocked. Every table is laid. Every bed is made. (+4 Mind)
It goes out, and somewhere far off a bell rings once, in reproach. (-2 luck)
You swim on, and dream for a year about the lanterns. (+2 align)

events.text: At the end of the drowned street is a house with one lantern out, the lantern of a family that was not home when the star fell. A letter on the table, never sent, asks whoever reads it to tell them the town waited.

effects.log: It takes a long search. Their descendants are fishermen on a coast below, and do not believe a word, and keep the letter anyway. (+8 align, +3 Mind)
You light it. The whole drowned town seems to sigh, and the lanterns burn steadier. (+5 align, +2 luck)

choices.text: Take the letter as a curiosity

effects.log: You keep it in a drawer. Sometimes the drawer is warm. (+2 Mind)

events.text: In the deepest hall of the Tomb of the Nameless Emperor, the first Immortal Sovereign, who had his name scraped off every wall in the heavens, the coffin lid stands a finger's width open. Light comes out of the gap. It is the colour of a name.
events.arc: The Name on the Inside of the Lid

effects.log: You slide the lid. The coffin is empty. On the inside of the lid, carved small, is the one name the Sovereign kept. (+5 Mind)
You push it shut, gently. The tomb is darker afterwards, and quieter, and somehow grateful. (+5 align)
You glimpse half a character before your eyes water. Half a name is a dangerous thing to carry. (+3 Mind, -2 luck)

events.text: The Nameless Emperor's name is in your head, and it is heavy. Whenever you think it, the stones of the tomb lean toward you. You understand: the name is a key. Whoever says it aloud in the Tomb could wake whatever the Sovereign put to sleep here.
events.arc: The Name on the Inside of the Lid

effects.log: You never say it. It sits in you like a stone in a river, and the river goes round. (+5 Mind, +3 align)

choices.text: Say it, once, in the deepest hall

effects.log: The tomb wakes. Something old and very polite asks what you want. You ask for nothing, and it goes back to sleep, impressed. (+6 Mind, +40 fame)

choices.text: Write it down for the Celestial Ministries

effects.log: The Court seals the paper in a box inside a box inside a vault. A minister thanks you in a shaking voice. (+20 fame, -2 align)

events.text: An immortal of great age comes to you, having heard you came back from the Tomb with something. The immortal is the Sovereign's last servant, alive all this time, and asks one thing: to hear the name, once, before dying.
events.arc: The Name on the Inside of the Lid

effects.log: You whisper it. The old servant closes their eyes and smiles, and the next morning is gone, very peacefully. (+6 align, +3 Mind)
The servant bows, understanding perfectly, and leaves you a ring that belonged to the Sovereign. (+5 luck, +2 Mind)

events.text: Half a name is worse than none. The half-character you saw in the Tomb of the Nameless Emperor comes back in dreams and pulls at you like a hook. You will have to go back for the rest of it, or tear it out.
events.arc: The Name on the Inside of the Lid

choices.text: Go back and read the rest

effects.log: You go back and read the whole name, and it settles in you, and the dreams stop. (+5 Mind)

choices.text: Tear it out of your memory

ok.log: You tear it out. Something is missing afterwards, small and sharp. You do not know what. (+3 align, +3 Mind)

fail.log: It will not come out. You carry half a name for the rest of your life. (-3 luck, +2 Mind)

events.text: The Tomb of the Nameless Emperor is guarded by an army: ten thousand immortals of fired clay, each a portrait of someone who served the first Sovereign, each holding a weapon of real jade. As you walk past, one of them turns its head.

effects.log: It cannot speak. It points down a side passage, and waits. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Walk on as if you did not see

ok.log: You walk on. Behind you, the head turns back. (+3 luck)

fail.log: Ten thousand heads turn at once. You run, and only just make it out. (-15 health)

effects.log: You bow. Ten thousand clay heads bow back, very slowly, in a sound like a landslide. (+5 align, +2 luck)

events.text: Down the side passage is a single clay soldier, cracked across the chest, a different face from the rest: plain, tired, smiling. Inside the crack, something is still alive. A real immortal, sealed in clay as a punishment, a hundred thousand years.

ok.log: The clay falls away. A very stiff, very surprised immortal stands up and asks what year it is. You do not know how to answer. (+8 align, +30 fame)

fail.log: The clay cracks but holds. The face inside smiles wider. You will need a better tool. (-8 health, +2 Mind)

choices.text: Ask what the punishment was for

effects.log: The clay creaks a single word: "Laughing." You find you would like to know at what. (+3 Mind)
You leave. The smile stays with you longer than the tomb does. (+1 luck)

events.text: The immortal you broke out of the clay has been learning the new heaven, one astonishment at a time. Today they come to you with their first question that is not about the world: what was the joke? They have forgotten what they were laughing at.

effects.log: They laugh until they sit down. It is not the same joke, they say, but it is the same laugh. (+5 charm, +4 align)

choices.text: Take them back to the Tomb to find it

effects.log: In the deepest hall you find a carving of the first Sovereign slipping on a step. The freed immortal laughs for a whole day. (+4 Mind, +30 fame)

events.text: In the Abyss of Ten Thousand Demons, where the Demon Realm throws what even it cannot keep, there is a voice at the bottom of a well of chains. It knows your name. It says it was here before the Demon Realm and will be here after, and that it is very bored, and would you talk.

effects.log: You talk for a month. It is the cleverest thing you have ever met, and the loneliest. (+5 Mind)
"A question somebody stopped asking," it says. You do not understand, and then, later, you do. (+4 Mind)
You leave. Its laughter follows you up a thousand chains. (+3 align)

events.text: The prisoner of the Abyss has made you an offer, as you knew it would. It knows a way out of the Abyss for itself, and in return for one link of its chain undone it will teach you anything you ask. It has never once lied to you. You are not sure that means anything.

effects.log: The link falls. The prisoner thanks you, sincerely, and teaches you something you should not know. Far above, the Demon Realm shivers. (+8 Mind, -8 align)
You refuse. The prisoner says, "Good. I hoped you would." You are not sure whether to be relieved. (+5 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Ask what it would do outside

effects.log: "Ask," it says. "Just ask. Everybody, everything. I have so many questions." (+4 Mind)

events.text: You come to the well of chains once more, to say goodbye. The prisoner has a gift ready: a question, the one it was made of, written on a scrap of light. "Carry it," it says. "Do not answer it. Just carry it out of here, so it is somewhere else."

effects.log: You carry it up the chains and out of the Abyss, and set it on the wind. Below, in the world of mortals, a child asks it of a teacher. (+6 Mind, +4 align)
You read it. You will spend the rest of a very long life not answering it, and it will make you wiser. (+8 Mind)

events.text: The link you undid has not been forgotten. In the Abyss the chains are louder now, and the prisoner's voice is nearer the top of the well. A Demon Duke comes to your door with a question of their own: who loosened it?

effects.log: The Duke stares, then laughs, then makes you go down with a hammer and put the link back. It takes ten years. (-5 health, +5 align)

choices.text: Go down and bind it tighter yourself

ok.log: You go down and bind it with your own qi. The prisoner says, almost fondly, "Well done." (+5 Mind)

fail.log: The chain bucks in your hands and throws you up the well. The Duke binds it, scowling. (-20 health)

events.text: The Abyss of Ten Thousand Demons answers anyone who shouts. Most of the echoes are only echoes. Yours is not: it shouts back in your voice, a moment early, saying things you were about to say, then things you never would.

effects.log: Your echo shouts it back, then something cruel, then nothing. (+3 align)
Your echo shouts on without you for an hour, and then, uncertain, stops. (+3 Mind)
You climb out. For a decade you sometimes hear yourself a moment early. (+2 luck)

events.text: Your echo has climbed out of the Abyss after you. It wears your face, roughly, as if from memory. It does everything you would do if you had never once been kind, and it is doing it under your name.

ok.log: You corner it on a drifting isle. It is you, and it is not, and when you strike it, it becomes a sound, and is gone. (+5 Mind, +20 fame)

fail.log: It fights exactly as you do and knows it. You both limp away. (-18 health)

choices.text: Go and undo what it did

effects.log: You spend a decade apologising for things you did not do. You learn a great deal about what you might have been. (+6 align, +3 Mind)
You sit across from yourself and talk. By dawn the echo is quieter, and by the next dawn it is only an echo again. (+6 Mind)

events.text: An expedition of seven immortals went into the Abyss of Ten Thousand Demons nine years ago and has not come back. Six of their lamps are still lit on the shelf at the Abyss gate; one has gone out. The families ask, in every faction, who will go in.

effects.log: You take a coil of starlight rope, a lamp and the names of seven strangers. (+4 align)
You pay a Demon General to go. The general comes back with nobody and a strange look. (+2 merit, -2 align)

choices.text: Light the seventh lamp again, and wait

effects.log: You light it. It burns. Nobody can say what that means. (+2 luck)

events.text: Four hundred spans down, in a cave lit by demon-fire, you find the six living immortals: unhurt, comfortable, and unwilling to leave. A demon of the Abyss has been telling them stories for nine years, and they want to hear how the stories end.

effects.log: You listen. It is a very good story. You have to tear yourself away at the end of the third year. (+5 Mind, +3 charm)

ok.log: You shout the end of the story before the demon can tell it. The spell breaks. The six immortals blink like sleepers and follow you up. (+8 align, +40 fame)

fail.log: The demon simply starts a new story. You stay a year before you can pull them out. (+4 align, -8 health)

choices.text: Ask the demon to let them go

effects.log: The demon, who only wanted listeners, sighs and lets them go, if you promise to come back for the ending. (+5 align)

events.text: You promised the storytelling demon of the Abyss you would come back for the ending. It is waiting, by its fire, with the six rescued immortals' empty cushions still around it.

effects.log: The ending is sad and right and you cry in the Abyss of Ten Thousand Demons, which no one has done for an age. The demon is very pleased. (+6 Mind, +4 align)

choices.text: Bring it a story of your own instead

effects.log: You tell it your life. It listens without moving, and at the end asks if it can keep it. (+5 charm, +5 align)

events.text: {npc}, one of the immortals who came to your isle to be taught, finds you at dawn on the edge of the cloud. {He} has trained under you for years, {he} says, and has learned a great deal, and does not know whether {he} has learned anything that is true. {He} would like to know what you actually believe.

effects.log: You talk until noon. {npc} listens without interrupting, then goes off to sit alone on a rock for a month. (+3 Mind)
{npc} frowns, and then nods, and from that day on trains as if someone were watching. (+3 prestige)
{npc} has never been asked. {He} answers badly, and then better, and then very well. (+4 Mind)

events.text: {npc} comes back from {his} rock. {He} has found a flaw in what you taught: small, honest, real. {He} lays it before you in front of the other disciples, not to shame you, only because {he} cannot pretend {he} has not seen it.

effects.log: You thank {npc} and change the teaching. The other disciples watch you do it and never forget. (+6 prestige, +4 align)

choices.text: Show {him} why it is not a flaw

ok.log: You show it. {npc} sees it, all at once, and laughs out loud for joy. (+5 Mind, +4 prestige)

fail.log: Your answer does not hold. {npc} is too kind to say so. Everyone notices. (-3 prestige)

choices.text: Tell {him} to raise it in private next time

effects.log: {npc} bows. {He} never raises anything in public again, and the isle is a little quieter. (+2 prestige, -2 align)

events.text: The other disciples have started bringing their doubts to {npc} before they bring them to you. {He} is teaching, without meaning to. Some of your older disciples think it is disrespectful.

choices.text: Make {npc} an elder of the isle

effects.log: {npc} is appalled and then very good at it. Your isle grows a second voice. (+8 prestige)

choices.text: Let it go on as it is

effects.log: It goes on. Your isle has two teachers, one official. It is the happiest the isle has been. (+4 prestige, +3 align)

events.text: Two of your immortal disciples have found the same thing on the same day: a manual in a grotto under your isle, left by whoever lived there before the isle was yours. Each found it first. Each will not let go of their end of it.

choices.text: Take it, and teach it to both

effects.log: You take it, read it twice and teach it to both of them together, slowly. Neither forgives you for a decade. Both learn it. (+4 prestige)
They duel. The loser trains so hard afterwards that a year later they are better than the winner. (+3 prestige, +2 Mind)
You burn it. Two shocked disciples. One clean isle. (+2 align, -2 prestige)
