events.text: The manual from the grotto was not finished. The last page says: "The rest is under the other isle." There is no other isle in sight. But the two disciples are already, together, looking.

effects.log: You go. It takes eleven years and three isles, and the two disciples become inseparable. (+6 prestige, +4 Mind)
They go alone and come back a decade later, sunburnt and friends, with the second half. (+5 prestige)

events.text: With both halves of the old manual, your two disciples have found its author: an immortal who lived on your isle a hundred thousand years ago and wrote the manual so that, one day, two people would have to work together to read it.

choices.text: Name a hall after the author

effects.log: The hall of the Unknown Author stands on your isle, and every disciple who enters is given a partner. (+8 prestige)

choices.text: Write a manual of your own the same way

effects.log: You write it in two halves and hide them. Somebody, in a hundred thousand years, will have to make a friend. (+5 Mind, +4 align)

events.text: A procession of the Celestial Ministries lands on your isle: an inspector, twelve clerks, and a scroll declaring that every immortal sect must be registered, taxed in merit and inspected once a millennium. The inspector looks around your halls with an expression of mild pain.

effects.log: The inspector sees everything, including the leaking roof and the goat. The report is surprisingly kind. (+4 prestige, +2 align)
The inspector leaves. The Court sends a sterner one in ten years. (+3 prestige, -2 luck)

choices.text: Host the inspector as a guest

effects.log: Tea, a walk, a game of go. The inspector forgets to inspect anything and goes away happy. (+3 charm, +2 prestige)

events.text: The sterner inspector arrives with a hundred Celestial Officers and orders your disciples registered, by name and realm, in the Court's book. Your disciples look at you.

effects.log: You register them. The Court is satisfied. Two disciples quietly leave the isle that year, and are not heard of again. (+2 prestige, -3 align)

choices.text: Refuse, and stand at the gate

ok.log: You stand at the gate. Nobody passes. After a day the inspector bows and leaves, and your isle is never inspected again. (+10 prestige, +40 fame)

fail.log: The officers do not need to pass you. They wait until you tire, and then they register everyone anyway. (-15 health, -3 prestige)

effects.log: The inspector considers, and writes one name. Your disciples will tell the story for ten thousand years. (+6 prestige, +4 align)

events.text: The kind report of the first inspector has done strange things. Other inspectors of the Celestial Ministries have started stopping at your isle on their way past, to rest and drink tea and complain about the Court.

effects.log: Your isle becomes the place where tired officials come to breathe. You hear everything first. (+5 prestige, +4 Mind)
You charge them in favours. Within a century half the Court owes you something small. (+6 prestige, -2 align)

events.text: Your isle has drifted. Overnight, quietly, with all your halls and disciples on it, it has slid four days east, and now hangs over the cloud border of the Demon Realm. In the morning a Demon Duke is standing on your outer terrace, very politely asking whose island this is.

choices.text: Say it is yours, and it stays

effects.log: The Duke smiles. "Then you are my neighbour," the Duke says, and leaves a gift, which is worse. (+3 prestige)
It takes every disciple a year of pushing qi. Your isle goes home, and your disciples are stronger in the shoulders. (+4 prestige, -10 health)
The Duke has never been asked to tea. The Duke comes back every year. (+3 charm, +2 prestige)

events.text: Living on the Demon border has changed your isle. Your disciples are tougher, warier, and some of them have friends among the demons. The Celestial Ministries have begun to call your isle a nest of demons, and some factions have stopped sending you visitors.

choices.text: Keep the isle where it is

effects.log: You keep it. Your isle becomes the only place where a demon and an immortal can sit at one table. (+6 prestige, +4 align)

choices.text: Move the isle away from the border

effects.log: You move it. The friendships fade. The Court is pleased. (+3 prestige, -3 align)

events.text: Word has come: the Celestial Ministries and the Demon Realm, both tired of a border skirmish that has lasted three centuries, will talk. Neither will go to the other. Both have asked to meet on your isle.

effects.log: They talk under your roof for a year. They do not make peace. They make a truce, and set its stone on your terrace. (+15 prestige, +60 fame)
On the last day, you speak. Both sides are angry with you. The truce holds anyway. (+10 prestige, +6 align)

events.text: {npc} has been sitting in your meditation hall for nine years without moving, and this morning {he} opened {his} eyes and the hall was full of a Dao you have never touched. It is {his} own. It is not yours. You did not teach it.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Found a Dao

effects.log: You bow. {npc} goes red to the ears, and bows back much lower. The whole isle hears of it by dusk. (+6 prestige, +4 align)
{npc} is horrified and then delighted. You are a terrible student. You learn anyway. (+5 Mind, +4 prestige)
You watch {npc} for a year, and are proud, and a little jealous, and keep both to yourself. (+3 Mind)

events.text: Other sects have heard of {npc}'s Dao. The Jade Void Sect has sent an invitation. The Star Sea Pavilion has sent two. They are offering {him} things your isle cannot.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Found a Dao

effects.log: {npc} thinks about it for a season and stays. "You told me I could go," {he} says. "That is why I stay." (+8 prestige)
{npc} stays, because you asked. You are not sure that was fair. (+4 prestige, -2 align)
{npc} finds out, and is angry for a year, and then oddly touched. (+3 prestige)

events.text: Somebody on your isle has been writing everything down. You find the ink-stains on {npc}'s sleeve, and a fold of paper in {his} room in a code you know: the Star Sea Pavilion's.

effects.log: {npc} goes white and tells you everything: {he} was placed here by the Pavilion, years ago, and has come to love the isle. (+3 align)
For a decade the Pavilion believes your isle is far poorer and far stranger than it is. (+3 Mind, +2 prestige)
{npc} goes without a word. Your other disciples are frightened for a year. (-3 prestige)

events.text: {npc}, who confessed to spying for the Star Sea Pavilion, asks what {he} should do now. The Pavilion is expecting a report. If it does not come, it will send someone to ask why.

effects.log: {npc} sends true reports. The Pavilion is puzzled by a sect with nothing to hide, and stops paying for them. (+4 align, +3 prestige)
You go together and lay the code on the Pavilion Master's desk. The Master laughs, and releases {npc} from service. (+5 prestige, +20 fame)

events.text: Your isle is known now, a little. Immortals of every faction drift past to look at it. A disciple suggests that once a century you give an open lecture, on the outer terrace, for anyone at all.

effects.log: Forty immortals come, and three demons in disguise, and a crane. You speak on the one thing you are sure of. (+6 prestige, +20 fame)
Your disciple gives it, terrified, and is wonderful. The isle's name spreads in a new voice. (+5 prestige)
Your isle stays quiet. Your disciples train in peace, and grumble. (+2 Mind)

events.text: Your second open lecture draws four hundred immortals. Among them is a Grand Elder of the Jade Void, an old reader of the Star Sea and someone in a plain grey robe whom nobody can quite look at directly. Halfway through, the one in grey raises a hand.

ok.log: The question is a hard one. Your answer is not perfect, but it is honest, and the one in grey nods and vanishes. Your isle is famous by morning. (+12 prestige, +60 fame)

fail.log: You stumble. The one in grey waits, kindly, and then answers it for you, which is worse. (+3 Mind, +3 prestige)

effects.log: The terrace goes quiet. The one in grey smiles. "Good," they say, and leave. You are thought very wise. (+8 prestige, +4 align)

events.text: The sky over your isle is going dark in a shape you know: a tribulation. It is coming for {npc}, who is ready, mostly, and is standing very straight at the cloud's edge, trying not to look at you.

effects.log: You watch from the hall door. {npc} takes nine bolts and stands up after every one. (+6 prestige)
You stand beside {npc}. A tribulation does not like a second target; it argues with itself, and comes down softer. (+5 align, -10 health)

choices.text: Read the storm and call out its rhythm

ok.log: You call every bolt a breath before it falls. {npc} dances through them. (+5 prestige, +4 Mind)

fail.log: You call one bolt wrong. {npc} takes it full on, and passes anyway, and never mentions it. (+3 prestige, -2 luck)

events.text: {npc}, who passed the tribulation on your isle, has a lightning-mark on {his} wrist now, and a very calm way of standing. {He} asks if {he} may build a small pavilion where the storm came down.

effects.log: You build it together. Afterwards every disciple who faces a storm on your isle faces it from that pavilion. (+6 prestige, +3 charm)
{npc} builds it alone, slowly, and badly, and it is the most loved building on the isle. (+5 prestige, +3 align)

events.text: Your understanding of the Sword Dao has grown so deep that this morning your sword would not come out of its sheath. It is not stuck. It is refusing. The Sword Dao has decided that, for you, drawing a sword has become a lie.
events.arc: The Sword That Would Not Be Drawn

effects.log: For a year you walk the Upper Realm with a sheathed sword, and win two duels with the scabbard. (+5 Mind)

ok.log: It comes, screaming. The edge is fine. Something in you is not, quite. (+5 fame, -8 health)

fail.log: It does not come. The Sword Dao turns its face from you for a while. (-10 health, -2 Mind)

choices.text: Ask the sword what it wants

effects.log: It wants, as far as you can tell, to be the idea of a sword, and not the thing. (+4 Mind)

events.text: A sword immortal of the Jade Void has heard that you fight with a sheathed sword, and is insulted, and comes to prove that the Sword Dao is a sharp thing or nothing at all.
events.arc: The Sword That Would Not Be Drawn

ok.log: You touch {npc}'s wrist with the sheath, once. {npc} looks at the touch for a long time and goes home without another word. (+5 Mind, +30 fame)

fail.log: {npc} cuts your sheath in two. Your sword, inside, is laughing. (-12 health, +3 Mind)

effects.log: You decline. {npc} calls you a coward and stays a month to argue, and leaves less certain. (+3 Mind, +2 align)

events.text: Your sword comes out of its sheath on its own one evening, without you, and stands point down in the clouds in front of you, humming. It has decided the lie is over. It is ready, now, for whatever the Sword Dao will make of you next.
events.arc: The Sword That Would Not Be Drawn

effects.log: It fits your hand as if it had never left. Something has finished. (+6 Mind)
You leave it in the clouds. It stands there for a hundred years, and immortals come to look at it, and some of them learn. (+5 align, +40 fame)

events.text: An immortal who walks the Sword Dao finds you on a cloud road and is courteous, and very sure: the blade is only a sword that has forgotten its manners. {npc} would like to debate it. Up here a debate between Daos can last a century.

effects.log: {npc} sits down on the road. So do you. Clouds pile up behind you both, waiting to pass. (+3 Mind)

ok.log: One cut, through the cloud beside {npc}. The cloud stays cut for a year. {npc} bows. (+30 fame)

fail.log: {npc} catches your cut on two fingers, and smiles, and keeps walking. (-8 health)

effects.log: "Another time," you say. {npc} nods, as if a hundred years were nothing. (+2 luck)

events.text: The debate with {npc} has gone on for eleven years. You have both said everything twice. Today {npc} says, "A sword is a question. A blade is an answer." You find you cannot argue with it.

effects.log: {npc} is so surprised that {he} concedes one back, and you both learn more in that hour than in eleven years. (+6 Mind)
"Then what is a hand?" you ask. The debate goes on, gladly, another eleven years. (+5 Mind, +2 charm)

events.text: {npc}, your old opponent in the debate of sword and blade, is dying, which immortals rarely do: an old wound, finally due. {He} asks you to come and finish the argument.

effects.log: {npc} wins, and knows you let {him}, and laughs, and that is how {he} goes. (+6 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Go, and argue to the end

effects.log: You argue to the last breath. {npc} goes out smiling, mid-sentence, about to make a very good point. (+6 Mind, +4 charm)

events.text: A small isle near yours is dying. Its pines are grey, its spring has gone sour, and the old immortal who lives there is sitting very still under the last green tree. The Dao of Life in you aches like a pulled muscle just looking at it.

choices.text: Ask the old immortal what happened

effects.log: "I stopped wanting to," the old one says. "The isle noticed." (+4 Mind)

choices.text: Pour your Dao into the isle

effects.log: You pour Life into it for a year. The pines green. The spring runs. You are tired in a way that takes a decade to lift. (+6 align, -10 health)
You leave it. The Dao of Life in you is quieter for a year, like a sulking child. (+2 Mind, -2 luck)

events.text: The old immortal on the withered isle is dying of having lived too long, a hundred and ninety thousand years. The Dao of Life could keep the immortal alive. It would mean tying the old one's life to yours.

effects.log: You tie them. The old immortal lives, and wakes some mornings with your dreams. You are more than one person now, a little. (+6 align, -200 years of life)
You sit with the old one until the end, and the end is gentle, and the isle greens a little afterwards, as if in thanks. (+5 Mind, +4 align)

choices.text: Ask the old immortal what they want

effects.log: They want, it turns out, to see one more spring. You make sure they do. (+5 align, +2 charm)

events.text: The isle you healed is too alive now: vines over the paths, flowers in the cracks of the roofs, a forest where there was a garden. Life, once started, does not know when to stop. The Dao of Life in you has the same problem.

ok.log: You sit in the forest a year until the forest and you both learn the word "enough". The isle settles into an orchard. (+6 Mind)

fail.log: It will not learn. The isle becomes a jungle that drifts off on its own, happy. (+3 Mind, +2 luck)

effects.log: You let it. The isle becomes the greenest place in the Upper Realm, and impossible to land on. (+5 align, +100 years of life)

events.text: Your Dao of Death has grown deep enough to be noticed. Tonight a boat comes out of the mist at the edge of the clouds: black, long, with one pale lantern, and in it a hooded figure who rows the dead across. The Ferryman is very tired, and wants an apprentice.

effects.log: "Rowing," says the Ferryman. "And listening. Mostly listening." (+4 Mind)
The Ferryman nods and rows away. The lantern lingers in the mist for a long time. (+2 align)
You step in. The boat does not rock. The water underneath is not water. (+5 Mind)

events.text: You row for the Ferryman for one night. The dead are not frightening. They are mostly surprised, and some are angry, and one is a mortal you knew, very long ago, below, who recognises you and laughs.

effects.log: You talk the whole way across. On the far side, they step off lightly, and wave. (+6 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Row in silence, as the Ferryman does

effects.log: You row in silence. You understand why the Ferryman is so tired, and why the Ferryman does not stop. (+6 Mind)
You turn the boat round with the acquaintance still in it. The Ferryman takes the oars from you, gently, and rows on. (-4 luck, +3 Mind)

events.text: The Ferryman has come again, rowing slower than before. The Ferryman would like to stop, and has rowed for a very long time, and asks whether you would take the oars, not for a night, but for a while: a century, perhaps.

choices.text: Take the oars for a century

effects.log: You row a century. It changes you. When you give the oars back, the Ferryman has rested, and you are very quiet. (+10 Mind, +6 align)

choices.text: Find the Ferryman a different helper

effects.log: You find a young immortal, sad and kind, who is glad of the work. The Ferryman is grateful. (+5 align, +3 charm)
The Ferryman nods and rows on, slower. You watch the lantern out of sight. (+2 Mind)

events.text: The Dao of the Void is making room in you. This morning you cannot remember the face of the one who raised you. It is not grief; there is simply a clean space where it was, and the space is very peaceful, and you are frightened.

choices.text: Stop meditating on the Void for a while

effects.log: You stop. Nothing more goes. The face does not come back. (+3 align)

choices.text: Let the Void take what it wants

effects.log: You let it. More rooms empty. You have never been so clear, or so alone. (+8 Mind, -4 charm)

choices.text: Write down everything you still remember

effects.log: You write for a year. It is the longest thing you have ever written. (+4 Mind)

events.text: The book of everything you remember is finished. Reading it back, you find things in it you have forgotten writing: the smell of a kitchen, the name of a dog, a song. The Void did not take them. It kept them for you, somewhere quiet.

effects.log: You read it to the clouds. By the end the empty rooms in you are furnished, lightly, again. (+5 Mind, +4 charm)

choices.text: Give the book to the Void

effects.log: You let the pages go into the dark. You remember them better than ever. (+8 Mind)

events.text: You are almost empty now. There is a great deal of room in you, and in that room, today, someone has come to sit: an immortal who also walks the Void, much further along, who has lost everything and is perfectly content, and who asks you, very kindly, whether you are sure.

effects.log: The other Void-walker nods, and the two of you sit in the empty room together for a century, perfectly content. (+10 Mind, -4 charm)
You start with the dog. Then the kitchen. Then the song. The other Void-walker smiles and goes. (+5 align, +5 charm)

events.text: You have been meditating on the Dao of Time, and now it is the same hour again. A plum petal falls past your face. Then the same petal falls past your face. You have lived this hour, by your own count, eleven times.

effects.log: You try every way of living one hour. On the forty-first you laugh at a joke nobody told. (+5 Mind, +3 charm)
You sit through the hour a hundred times until the hour gets bored and lets you go. (+6 Mind)

choices.text: Find what in the hour is wrong

effects.log: There is a thing in the hour that does not belong: a footprint in the snow, too small, and no snow. (+4 Mind)

events.text: The footprint in your repeating hour belongs to a small, lost thing: a moment that broke off a mortal's life below and drifted up, looking for its way home. Every time the hour repeats, the moment has a little less of itself left.

choices.text: Carry it back to its time

ok.log: You carry the moment down the years like a lantern and fit it back where it broke. Somewhere below, an old man suddenly remembers his wedding. (+8 align, +4 Mind)

fail.log: It slips at the last year. You fit it into the wrong life. Somebody below remembers a wedding they never had, fondly. (+3 align, +2 Mind)

choices.text: Keep it, so it does not fade

effects.log: You keep the moment in your sleeve. On cold nights it is warm, and smells of rice wine and red paper. (+4 luck, -2 align)

events.text: Time owes you, now. It shows it the way Time does: one morning the hour in which you were born comes up out of the past and stands in front of you, small and loud and very new, and waits to see what you will do with it.

effects.log: You live your first hour again, all of it, and come out of it understanding something you will never be able to say. (+8 Mind, +100 years of life)
You let it go. Some things should only happen once. (+5 align, +4 Mind)

events.text: You lit a small fire on your isle to meditate on the Dao of Flame, and it has not gone out. That was three years ago. It has eaten nothing, grown a little, and now has opinions. It is creeping toward the neighbour's orchard.
events.arc: The Fire That Would Not Go Out

effects.log: It is not a good listener. It is, however, a very good arguer. You hold it back for a year by argument alone. (+4 Mind)

ok.log: You smother it. It goes out, sulking, and relights in your chest for a week. (+3 Mind)

fail.log: It is not smothered. It is offended. The orchard catches. (-10 health, -3 align)

effects.log: You give it your oldest regrets. It burns them happily and stays where it is. (+5 align)

events.text: The fire is a person now, almost. It has a name it chose itself, which is a crackle, and a temper, and it follows you around your isle like a large affectionate dog that is also on fire.
events.arc: The Fire That Would Not Go Out

effects.log: It becomes the hearth of your isle. Everyone who sits by it says it is the warmest fire in the heavens. (+5 align, +3 charm)
You lift it up and let it go. That night there is a new star, crackling. (+6 Mind, +30 fame)

events.text: An immortal of the Water Dao comes to your isle, very politely, to put your fire out. The fire, hearing, grows to the height of a pavilion. The Water immortal grows a lake. Your isle will not survive the conversation.
events.arc: The Fire That Would Not Go Out

effects.log: You stand between fire and water and steam for a day. At the end they are both too tired to fight, and agree to differ. (+5 align, -5 health)

ok.log: You argue that fire and water make tea. The Water immortal laughs, and stays for tea. (+5 Mind, +3 charm)

fail.log: You argue badly. The Water immortal puts the fire out, apologetically. It relights in your chest a year later. (+2 Mind)

events.text: On a bridge over a river of cloud, an immortal of the Dao of Earth stops you. {npc} has walked Earth for eighty thousand years and thinks Water is a Dao for those who never decided anything. {He} would like to hear you defend it.

effects.log: You talk about patience. {npc} talks about foundations. You both talk until the river freezes over. (+4 Mind)
You stand on the bridge until {npc} gets bored. It takes three years. {npc} admits that was a good argument. (+5 Mind, +3 luck)
You walk round. {npc} shouts after you that that is exactly the problem. You agree. (+2 charm)

events.text: {npc} of the Earth Dao has come back with a stone that has never been worn down by anything. {He} sets it in your river and dares the Water Dao to move it.

choices.text: Let the river take a thousand years

effects.log: You and {npc} sit by the river for a thousand years. At the end the stone is a pebble and you are friends. (+8 Mind, +4 charm)

choices.text: Move it now, with your whole Dao

ok.log: Water flows under the stone and lifts it like a leaf. {npc} sits down very hard. (+6 Mind, +30 fame)

fail.log: The stone does not move. The river goes round. {npc} looks smug for a century. (+3 Mind)

effects.log: "You see?" says {npc}. "Yes," you say. "That is the whole of it." {He} is quiet for a long time. (+5 Mind)

events.text: Ever since your Dao of Thunder deepened, a small storm has followed you about the Upper Realm. It is not dangerous. It is only loud, and it rains on whatever you are standing next to. At the Jade Court, the ministers have begun to sit away from you.

effects.log: You train it for a year. It learns to stay above you and to thunder only when you laugh. (+4 Mind, +2 charm)
You send it away. It goes, and stops at the edge of sight, and waits. (+2 Mind)
You let it rain. Your isle is the greenest in the heavens and nobody visits. (+3 luck, -2 charm)

events.text: Someone else's tribulation is coming down on a nearby isle: a young immortal, not ready, who will not survive it. Your little storm, hearing the thunder, has gone very quiet. It is waiting to see what you will do.

ok.log: You step under it. The bolts know you, and slide off you like rain. The young immortal lives. (+10 align, +40 fame)

fail.log: You take it, and it takes a great deal of you. The young immortal lives. (-25 health, +8 align)

choices.text: Send your storm to meet it

effects.log: Your storm goes up and argues with the tribulation, thunder to thunder. The tribulation, confused, rains instead. (+6 align, +4 Mind)
Tribulations are a debt between one soul and the sky. The young immortal passes, barely. (+3 Mind)

events.text: You have been sitting on a stone on the Dao of Earth for twenty years. This morning the stone is a hill. By evening it will be a small mountain, and the floating village on the next isle is already in its shadow, and complaining.

effects.log: You stand up. The mountain stops growing, embarrassed. (+3 Mind)
You keep sitting. By the end of the year your mountain is the tallest in the Upper Realm, and the village has moved. (+6 Mind, -4 align)
You move to a bare isle. It grows a mountain there, happily, with nobody to mind. (+5 Mind, +2 align)

events.text: The mountain you sat into being has started to sit on you. It wants you to stay. The Dao of Earth is patient, and very heavy, and if you stay a thousand years more you will be a part of it, like the Jade Void's ancestor.

effects.log: You stay a hundred years, and then, very slowly, stand up, and the mountain lets you go, reluctantly, with a gift of its patience. (+8 Mind, +500 years of life)
You go. The mountain stays. It is still there, a monument to sitting. (+3 luck)

choices.text: Give the mountain back to the village

effects.log: You give the village the mountain's slopes. They terrace it and grow cloud-tea. (+6 align, +3 charm)

events.text: Since your Dao of Wind deepened, the wind brings you things. A leaf from a forest that burned below a thousand years ago. A child's paper kite. Today, a voice: somebody far off, crying, in a language you do not speak.

effects.log: You follow the wind for a month, across the Upper Realm, to its edge. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Send the wind back with comfort

effects.log: You send back the sound of rain on a roof. The crying, far off, stops. (+5 align)
You close them. The wind sulks and brings you nothing for a decade. (-2 luck)

events.text: At the far edge of the Upper Realm, where the wind comes in from wherever wind comes from, an immortal is sitting alone, crying, an exile of some realm you have never heard of, who came in on the wind a thousand years ago and has never been found.

effects.log: You sit for a year. The exile teaches you twelve words of a language that has no speakers. You teach eleven back. (+5 Mind, +5 align)

choices.text: Bring the exile home with you

effects.log: The exile comes, and stays, and starts to laugh again after a century. (+8 align, +3 charm)

events.text: The exile who came in on the wind wants to go back out on it. Out there, beyond the edge, the exile says, is the realm where they came from. It is very small now. The exile is the last of it, and would like to be the last of it there.

effects.log: You lift the exile on your Dao and let them go, out past the edge. The wind comes back alone, warm, and smelling of salt. (+8 align, +4 Mind)

choices.text: Go with them a little way

effects.log: You go as far as the wind will take you. What you see out there you will never be able to describe, and you try for ten thousand years. (+10 Mind)

events.text: The Dao of Karma has opened your eyes to the threads. Every immortal you pass trails them: fine red lines of debt and favour running off into the clouds. Your own are many. One of them is very thick, and very old, and it runs straight down, through the clouds, into the world below.

choices.text: Follow it down with your eyes

effects.log: It runs to a grave in a village you burned through once, long ago, below, in a hurry, for a reason that seemed good. (+4 Mind)
You pull. Somewhere far below, a candle goes out, and a dog barks. The thread does not move. (-2 luck, +2 Mind)
You look away. The thread is still there when you look back. Threads are patient. (+2 Mind)

events.text: The thick red thread of your old debt has a living end: the line of a family below whose fortunes you broke, centuries ago, without much thought. They have been poor ever since, honestly, steadily, the way karma is poor.

effects.log: You send down, quietly, a good harvest, a scholar's luck, a healthy grandchild, and keep sending for a century. The thread thins to a hair. (+8 align, -3 luck)
You cut it. The Dao of Karma recoils from you like a struck animal. Below, nothing changes at all. (-6 align, +4 Mind)
You cannot go down. You send a dream instead: you, at the family's door, bowing. The family wakes and argues about it at breakfast. (+5 align, +2 Mind)

events.text: Your debts are fewer now, and lighter. The Dao of Karma shows you a new thread, so thin you nearly missed it, running from you to a stranger in the Upper Realm you have never met. It is not a debt. Someone owes you, for something you never knew you did.

effects.log: A tired immortal opens the door, sees you, and bursts into tears: you once gave them water on the white stairs, and they have been looking for you for three thousand years. (+5 charm, +5 align)
You let it stand. Somewhere a stranger is grateful to you forever. It is a good feeling to carry. (+4 luck, +3 Mind)

events.text: Two immortals of the Nine Clouds Palace bring you a quarrel they have had for four thousand years, because word has spread that the Dao of Balance in you cannot lie. One says the other stole a recipe. The other says it was a gift. Both are telling the truth as they remember it.

effects.log: You weigh them for a month. In the end it was a gift and a theft both: one gave, the other took more. They split the recipe and are friends by spring. (+5 Mind, +4 align)
You refuse. The Dao of Balance in you approves, a little primly. The two go home still quarrelling. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Take the side of the weaker

effects.log: You favour the weaker one. The scale in your chest tilts, and does not quite come back. (+3 align, -2 Mind)

events.text: Word of your judgement has spread too far. Immortals queue at your isle with quarrels, a hundred at a time. The Dao of Balance in you is growing heavy and very cold, and you have stopped feeling anything about any of them.

choices.text: Close the door for a century

effects.log: You close it. You sit by the sea of clouds until you feel something again: boredom, at first, then joy. (+5 Mind, +4 charm)
You keep judging. You are always fair. Nobody on the isle laughs any more, including you. (+8 Mind, -6 charm)
You train twelve judges. Their judgements are worse than yours and much kinder. (+5 align, +20 fame)

events.text: The Dao of Balance has decided you are out of balance. It turns its scales on you: everything you are, weighed against everything you have done. You feel the scale in your chest begin, very slowly, to tilt.

ok.log: It weighs you to the last grain and comes to rest, exactly level. You laugh for the first time in a century. (+8 Mind, +6 charm)

fail.log: It tilts, and stays tilted, and you understand what you have been missing. You begin to put it right. (+4 Mind, +4 align)

effects.log: You go and do something wildly generous and slightly foolish. The scales, startled, level out. (+6 align, +4 charm)

events.text: Your Dao of Illusion has grown so fine that this morning you woke, made tea, walked to the edge of your isle, and found that you were still in bed. Or the bed was the illusion. You are no longer entirely sure which morning was yours.

effects.log: It hurts in both. That does not help as much as you hoped. (+3 Mind)
You live in both mornings for a month. In one you are kinder. You are not sure which one that is. (+5 Mind, -2 luck)

choices.text: Stop practising the Dao for a while

effects.log: You stop. The two mornings slowly become one. You are relieved, and a little sad. (+3 align)

events.text: Someone has noticed that there are two of you. An immortal of the Jade Court has seen you in two places on one day and has drawn conclusions, and now somewhere in the Upper Realm a rumour runs that you are not one immortal but a conspiracy.

choices.text: Show the Court both of you at once

effects.log: The Court is thrown into a magnificent panic. For a century, every minister checks twice who they are talking to. (+4 Mind, +30 fame)

choices.text: Fold the two back into one

ok.log: You fold them together like two pages of a book. You are one person again, with two mornings' worth of memories. (+6 Mind)

fail.log: They will not fold. One of you walks off into the clouds, waving. You do not know which one stayed. (+3 Mind, -3 luck)

effects.log: You let it. The conspiracy is much more feared than you ever were. (+3 luck, +2 charm)

events.text: You are one again, or think you are. The Dao of Illusion has left one gift: you can see, now, every illusion anyone in the Upper Realm is holding up. There are a great many. Most of them are holding up very small, frightened people.

effects.log: You leave them. Everybody needs a shell. You are gentler with everyone afterwards, and nobody knows why. (+6 align, +4 charm)

choices.text: Show one immortal what you see

effects.log: You show a proud minister what you see. The minister weeps, and is grateful, and is a better minister ever after. (+5 Mind, +3 align)

events.text: Practising the Dao of Space, you fold the distance between two isles too far, and the fold does not close. There is a door in the air now, about your height, and through it you can see a street in the world below, at night, with snow falling.

effects.log: You watch the street for a night. A baker opens a shop at dawn. A dog follows the baker. (+3 Mind, +2 align)
You step through and stand in the snow below for one breath, and the cold is real, and then the fold pulls you back. (+5 Mind, -5 health)
You close it. It takes a month. The edges of the fold are very sharp. (+3 Mind, -6 health)

events.text: The door you folded has been found, from the other side. A child below, out in the snow, has seen it, and has stood in front of it every night since, waiting, and tonight puts a hand through and waves.

effects.log: You wave. The child laughs and runs off to tell everyone. Nobody believes the child, and the child does not care. (+4 align, +3 charm)
You close it, gently, the way you would close a window on a sleeping house. (+3 Mind, +2 align)
You leave a peach from the Upper Realm. The child eats it, and lives to be a hundred and twelve. (+6 align)

events.text: The fold has grown. Through it, now, the whole snowy town below can see the Upper Realm, faintly, like a reflection on ice. They have started leaving offerings on the edge. The Celestial Ministries have sent you a stiff note.

ok.log: You close it with the whole of your Dao. The town below sees one last reflection and then only snow. They remember it for a thousand years. (+6 Mind, +3 align)

fail.log: It closes partway. The town can see the Upper Realm only on the coldest night of each year, and celebrates it. (+3 Mind, +4 charm)

effects.log: You write back that the town is very nice and the snow is beautiful. The Court sends a sterner note. You frame it. (+3 charm, +2 luck)

events.text: The Dao of Slaughter has started to talk. It is not loud. It sounds like a crowd of blades very far off, all saying the same word, and the word is a name: the name of an immortal you passed at the Jade Court today, who did nothing to you at all.
events.arc: The Voice of Ten Thousand Blades

effects.log: You ignore it. It says the name all night. In the morning it says a different one. (+3 Mind, -2 luck)
"No," you say aloud. The blades go quiet, surprised. They have not been refused in a long time. (+5 align)

choices.text: Go and find the immortal it named

effects.log: You find them. They are a gardener. You stand in their garden for a long time, and leave. (+4 align, +3 Mind)

events.text: The voice of the Dao of Slaughter has grown louder. It no longer asks. It shows you, in dreams, the quickest way to every throat in the Upper Realm, and wakes you smiling. You do not like the smile.
events.arc: The Voice of Ten Thousand Blades

ok.log: You set the ten thousand blades against each other in your heart. They fight a hundred years and fall silent. You are very tired, and free, and still strong. (+8 Mind, +8 align)

fail.log: The blades will not turn. You hold them back by will alone, every night, for as long as you walk this Dao. (+4 Mind, -10 health)

choices.text: Go somewhere with no one to harm

effects.log: You go to the farthest isle of the Upper Realm and sit there alone for a century, until the voice tires of having no one to name. (+6 Mind, +4 align)
You listen a little. You win every duel for a decade, and stop being invited anywhere. (+20 fame, -8 align)

events.text: The Dao of Slaughter in you is quiet now, a sheathed thing. An immortal comes to your farthest isle, haunted by the same voice, having heard that someone once made it stop.
events.arc: The Voice of Ten Thousand Blades

effects.log: You teach them. It takes a century, and is the hardest teaching you have ever done, and it works. (+8 align, +4 Mind)
You sit together. Two sheathed blades on one isle. It is enough, some days. (+5 align, +3 charm)

events.text: Once in ten thousand years the immortals hold the Debate of the Thousand Daos: every seeker of every Dao on a ring of floating lotus seats above the sea of clouds, arguing which Dao is the root of the others. This time, by lot, you are to speak first.
events.arc: The Debate of the Thousand Daos

choices.text: Argue that your Dao is the root

effects.log: You argue it hard. Half the ring agrees by the end, which has never happened. The other half will never forgive you. (+40 fame, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Argue that no Dao is the root

effects.log: You say they all grow from one ground nobody has seen. The ring is quiet a long time. (+6 Mind)

choices.text: Yield your turn to a nervous young seeker

effects.log: The young seeker stammers through it and is unexpectedly brilliant. The ring will remember them, not you. (+5 align, +2 charm)

events.text: The Debate has gone on a hundred years and narrowed to two speakers: you, and an ancient Dao Lord who has said nothing until now. The Dao Lord stands, looks at you, and asks a single question: "Why do you want to understand anything at all?"
events.arc: The Debate of the Thousand Daos

ok.log: You answer honestly. The Dao Lord bows, and sits, and the Debate ends there, which nobody has seen in a hundred thousand years. (+10 Mind, +80 fame)

fail.log: You answer, and it is not enough, and the Dao Lord smiles as if it were. You will be answering it for the rest of your life. (+6 Mind)

effects.log: The Dao Lord laughs out loud, for the first time anybody can remember, and says, "I was hoping someone would." (+6 Mind, +40 fame)
The ring is silent. The Dao Lord nods slowly. "Good," the Dao Lord says. "Then you can still learn." (+5 Mind, +4 align)

events.text: {npc} has been in the Upper Realm nine thousand years and has never found a Dao. Every one {he} has tried slides off {him} like rain. {He} asks whether {he} might sit near you and watch how you hold yours.

effects.log: {npc} sits for a year, watching. On the last day {he} says, "You do not hold it. It holds you." (+4 Mind)
"Perhaps there is nothing to find," you say. {npc} looks stricken, then oddly relieved. (+3 Mind, +2 align)
You send {npc} on to a wiser teacher. {He} goes, politely. You feel you have failed a test. (-2 luck)

events.text: {npc}, the seeker who never found a Dao, comes back after a century, and something has changed. {He} has found one: not one of the sixteen, but a small Dao nobody has named, the Dao of Waiting. {He} would like you to be the first to see it.

effects.log: It is very quiet and very beautiful, like snow settling. You understand something about patience that your own Dao never taught you. (+6 Mind, +3 align)

choices.text: Bring it before the Jade Court

effects.log: The Court argues for ten years whether a seventeenth Dao is permitted. {npc} waits, happily, through every day of it. (+40 fame, +3 charm)

events.text: In meditation you hear something crack, very small, like ice on a pond in spring: your Dao heart. There is a hairline flaw in it, and through the flaw something old is looking in. It has your face, younger, and is angry about something you had forgotten.
events.arc: The Crack in the Dao Heart

effects.log: You seal it with qi. It holds, for now. Sometimes at night it ticks, like a cooling stove. (+2 Mind, -10 qi)
You look. Your younger face tells you, at length, everything you did wrong. Most of it is true. (+4 Mind, -5 health)
"To be heard once," it says, "by someone who will not argue." (+4 Mind)

events.text: Your younger self, looking in through the crack in your Dao heart, has finished saying everything. Now it is waiting. You understand that whatever you say next will either heal the crack or split the heart in two.
events.arc: The Crack in the Dao Heart

effects.log: You say it. The face weeps, and you weep, and the crack closes like a healed wound, leaving a scar that makes the heart stronger. (+8 Mind, +5 align)

choices.text: Say: I have done better since

ok.log: You tell it what you have done since. It listens, and is proud, and fades, and the crack is gone. (+6 Mind, +4 charm)

fail.log: It does not believe you. The crack widens a hair. You will have to prove it, slowly. (+3 Mind, -10 health)

effects.log: You hold your younger self in silence until it is calm. The crack stays, but the face behind it is at peace. (+6 Mind)

events.text: The crack you sealed in your Dao heart has opened again, all at once, in the middle of a duel at the Jade Court. Your younger face is in it, shouting, and your opponent has stepped back, very respectfully, to let you deal with it.
events.arc: The Crack in the Dao Heart

effects.log: You kneel in the middle of the Jade Court and listen to your younger self for an hour. Nobody laughs. When you stand, you are whole. (+8 Mind, +20 fame)
You seal it again. It holds. You lose the duel. (+2 Mind, -10 health)

events.text: A Dao Lord comes to your isle: one who has reached Perfect Dao and could become it, and has not, for reasons no one knows. The Dao Lord sits in your doorway like a stray cat and asks for nothing, and seems to be waiting for you to ask something.

choices.text: Ask why they have not become the Dao

effects.log: The Dao Lord smiles. "Because then nobody would sit in doorways," the Dao Lord says. You think about that for years. (+6 Mind)

choices.text: Ask how to reach Perfect Dao

effects.log: "You are already walking," the Dao Lord says. "Walk slower." You are irritated for a decade, and then grateful. (+5 Mind, +2 luck)
You bring tea. The Dao Lord drinks it, nods, and leaves at sunset. Your Dao is clearer for a century, and you do not know why. (+4 Mind, +4 align)

events.text: The Dao Lord who sat in your doorway comes back after a century to say goodbye: the Dao Lord has decided, at last, to become the Dao. They would like a witness. Nobody else has ever been asked.

effects.log: You watch an immortal become a law of the world. Afterwards you cannot describe it, only that the light changed, and stayed changed. (+10 Mind, +100 years of life)

choices.text: Ask them to wait one more day

effects.log: The Dao Lord laughs, and waits a day, and spends it with you on the edge of the clouds talking about nothing. Then goes. (+6 charm, +5 align)

events.text: Every expedition into the Tomb of the Nameless Emperor comes back with a different map. You have three of them, and they agree on nothing. You realise, laying them over one another, that the Tomb is not badly mapped: it is moving, slowly, like something turning over in its sleep.

effects.log: You spend a decade plotting the tomb's turns. It is walking. Very slowly, toward the Celestial Ministries. (+5 Mind)

choices.text: Sell the maps to whoever wants them

effects.log: The maps fetch a fortune. Three expeditions get lost with them. You feel bad about it. (-3 align, +3 luck)
You burn them. Some things should be found by accident. (+3 align)

events.text: The Tomb of the Nameless Emperor is walking toward the Celestial Ministries, a span a year. In nine thousand years it will arrive. Nobody at the Court believes you. The Tomb, as far as you can tell, is going home.

choices.text: Warn the Court until they listen

effects.log: It takes a century. Then the Court builds, very quietly, a great empty hall on its eastern edge, just in case. (+40 fame, +4 Mind)

choices.text: Go into the Tomb and ask it why

ok.log: In the deepest hall, the Tomb tells you, in a voice of shifting stone: it wants to see the throne once more. You promise to be there when it does. (+8 Mind, +5 align)

fail.log: The Tomb does not answer. It turns over in its sleep, and you are a long time finding the way out. (-15 health, +3 Mind)

effects.log: You let it walk. Nine thousand years is long even for you. You leave a note for whoever is alive then. (+3 Mind, +2 luck)

events.text: The tribulation that brought you through the last gate left a scar: a thin line of light down your back, like a crack in porcelain mended with gold. It does not hurt. When it rains, it hums. Other immortals look at it and then look away.

effects.log: You wear high collars for a century. The scar hums under the silk, faintly, and you grow used to it. (+2 luck)

choices.text: Ask an old immortal about it

effects.log: "The sky kept a piece of you," the old one says, "and left a piece of itself. Fair trade, usually." (+4 Mind)
You let it show. At the Jade Court, an immortal you have never met bows to it. (+20 fame)

events.text: On a night of heavy storm, the scar on your back answers the lightning. A bolt comes down out of a clear patch of sky, very gently, and touches you, and in that touch you understand the storm that made you, as if it had written you a letter.

effects.log: The storm, it turns out, was not trying to destroy you. It was asking whether you were sure. You find, now, that you are. (+8 Mind)
You hold out your hand and give the storm a little of your qi. It rumbles off, pleased. (+5 align, -10 qi)

events.text: The isle where your tribulation came down is not scorched any more. Something has grown in the crater: flowers with blue lightning in their petals, crackling softly in the wind. Nobody has ever seen them before. The Nine Clouds Palace has sent three alchemists to look.

effects.log: They study them for a decade and make one pill that tastes of thunder. They give it to you, in fairness. (+100 years of life, +2 Mind)
You send the alchemists away. The flowers are yours, and you sit among them in the evenings, humming. (+4 Mind, -2 charm)
They need storms. You promise them one, now and then. (+3 luck, +2 align)

events.text: The lightning-flowers have spread. Wherever an immortal's tribulation has fallen in the Upper Realm, the flowers are coming up, and immortals are going to sit in them, quietly, remembering their storms. Your crater is the oldest garden.

effects.log: Your crater becomes a place of pilgrimage. Immortals who were afraid of their next storm come and sit, and leave less afraid. (+8 align, +40 fame)
You tend them a century. The oldest grow tall, and their thunder deepens into music. (+6 Mind, +3 luck)

events.text: Something was born in your last tribulation. You did not notice at the time. It has been following you since: a small horse of storm-cloud and lightning, the size of a dog, that eats static and shies at kindness.

effects.log: You comb sparks out of the clouds for it. It eats them out of your hand and, very slowly, stops shying. (+4 align, +2 luck)

choices.text: Shoo it back into the sky

effects.log: You shoo it. It goes up into a cloud and sulks there, raining on you specifically. (+2 Mind)
It is far too small and very offended. You both end the day singed. (-6 health, +3 charm)

events.text: The thunder foal has grown. It is the size of a war-horse now, and you can ride it, and the Demon Realm has offered a fortress for it, and the Celestial Ministries a ministry. It looks at you as if it has an opinion.

effects.log: You refuse both. The foal, now a horse, butts you very hard in the chest, which you decide is affection. (+5 align, +3 charm)
You ask it. It walks to the edge of the clouds and looks at the storm-sky beyond for a long time. (+4 Mind)

events.text: The thunder horse wants to go home: into the storm-sky beyond the edge of the Upper Realm, where tribulations are born. It will not go without you, and it will not stay.

choices.text: Ride it out to the edge

effects.log: You ride it to the edge and it goes on without you, galloping into a storm the size of a world. It comes back to visit once a century. (+6 Mind, +100 years of life)

ok.log: You ride into the place where tribulations are born and come back with lightning in your hair and a new understanding of every storm. (+10 Mind, +60 fame)

fail.log: The storm-sky throws you back out like a pip. The horse comes after you, apologetic, and nudges you home. (-20 health, +4 Mind)

events.text: On a far isle a stranger's tribulation is gathering: an immortal you have never met, alone, sitting in the open, under a sky the colour of a bruise. Tribulations are a matter between one soul and the heavens. Everyone knows that. You are close enough to help.

ok.log: You stand under the storm with the stranger. It strikes you both and finds you both too stubborn. The stranger passes. (+8 align, -10 health)

fail.log: The storm turns on you as an intruder. You both barely live. The stranger passes, just. (-25 health, +6 align)

effects.log: You watch from a distance, ready to fetch help after. The stranger passes, by a hair. (+3 Mind)

choices.text: Call out the rhythm of the bolts

effects.log: You shout across the gap, bolt by bolt. The stranger hears, and dances, and passes. (+5 align, +3 Mind)

events.text: The stranger whose tribulation you helped with has found you. The Celestial Ministries have heard too, and the Ministries do not approve: interference with heaven's judgement. The stranger has come to stand beside you at the hearing.

effects.log: You argue that heaven's judgement was not interfered with, only argued with. The Court fines you, and quietly changes the rule. (+6 align, +20 fame)
You accept a century of confinement on a bare cloud. The stranger visits every year with soup. (+5 align, +4 charm)

events.text: In the last bolt of your tribulation, the one you nearly did not survive, there was a voice. You thought you imagined it. Now, years later, you hear it again in the thunder of an ordinary storm. It is saying your name, and then a word you do not know.
events.arc: The Voice in the Last Bolt

effects.log: It takes a decade. The word means, as near as you can tell, "again". (+5 Mind)
You ignore it. Every storm says your name now, politely, and you stop sleeping well in bad weather. (-2 luck)

choices.text: Ask other immortals whether they hear it

effects.log: Most do not. One old Sovereign does, and goes very pale. (+4 Mind)

events.text: The old Sovereign who also hears the voice in the thunder tells you what it is: the heaven itself, keeping count. Every soul that survives its storm is counted, and the count is nearing some number that the heaven has been waiting for since before the First Heaven fell.
events.arc: The Voice in the Last Bolt

choices.text: Ask what happens at the number

effects.log: "I do not know," the Sovereign says, "and I have been afraid of it for a hundred thousand years." You are afraid too, now. (+6 Mind)
The Sovereign looks at you a long time, then laughs, and seems, for the first time in an age, unafraid. (+5 align, +4 charm)

events.text: The Sovereign's tribulation was not lightning but silence: a weight of nothing that you held up until it gave. It is over. But some of the silence has stayed in you. Where you walk now, birds stop singing, and conversations falter, and do not start again.

effects.log: You practise for a century. Slowly, the silence around you becomes the kind people lean into, not away from. (+6 Mind, +4 charm)

choices.text: Go somewhere it does no harm

effects.log: You go to the edge of the heavens, where it is already quiet. The silence there is glad of the company. (+5 Mind, +3 align)
You sing, badly, at the Jade Court. The silence cracks. The Court is appalled and delighted. (+4 charm, +20 fame)

events.text: At the edge of the heavens the silence you carry has met another: the silence of a Sovereign who passed this way a hundred thousand years ago and never went back. It is not a person any more. It is a quiet that wants to be listened to.

effects.log: You listen for a year. At the end you know the name of the Sovereign who became a silence, and where they were born, and that they are not sad. (+8 Mind)
You carry it home inside your own silence. The Jade Court, for one day, is completely, peacefully still. (+5 align, +40 fame)

events.text: Every evening the clouds over the eastern isles are painted: peonies at dusk, cranes at moonrise, once a whole sea of carp that swam away into the night. You find the painter at last on a jade bridge, sleeves ink-black to the elbow: {npc}, who looks at you and then at the sky and says, "Hold still. You are the right colour."

effects.log: You hold still for an hour. That night the sky over the eastern isles is you, enormous and faintly surprised. (+4 charm)
{npc} hands you a brush the size of an oar and laughs at your first cloud, and keeps it anyway. (+3 Mind, +2 charm)
You walk on. That night the sky is grey, which has not happened in a thousand years. (+1 luck)

events.text: You have been painting the sky with {npc} for years. It turns out {he} paints because once, very long ago, {he} lost someone below, and painted the clouds so that, if they ever looked up, they would see something kind.

choices.text: Paint something for that lost one together

effects.log: You paint a lantern the size of a province. Somewhere below, perhaps, someone looks up. {npc} cries, and lets you see. (+5 align, +4 charm)
You talk until dawn and forget to paint. For once the sky is plain blue, and neither of you minds. (+5 charm, +3 Mind)

events.text: The Celestial Ministries have noticed the painted sky and do not approve: weather is a ministry, not an art. An order comes for {npc} to stop, or be confined to a grey cloud for ten thousand years.

choices.text: Argue for the painting before the Court

ok.log: You argue that the mortals below have started naming the paintings. The Court, outflanked by its own prayers, grants a licence. (+6 align, +30 fame)

fail.log: The Court will not hear it. You and {npc} paint at night instead, in secret, and it is the best work either of you ever does. (+4 charm, +2 luck)

choices.text: Paint the order itself into the sky

effects.log: You paint the Court's order across the whole sky, beautifully. The Court is so embarrassed it withdraws it. (+5 charm, +4 luck)

events.text: {npc} paints one last thing before you both stop for a century: two figures on a bridge of cloud, very small, under a sky full of lanterns. Then {he} puts the brush down and asks whether you would take the rite of Dao companions with {him}, under that sky.

choices.text: Take the rite under the painted sky

effects.log: You take the rite on the jade bridge where you met. Every immortal in the eastern isles looks up. Below, a whole province sees lanterns in the sky and makes wishes. (+6 charm, +300 years of life)

choices.text: Paint the sky for the rite yourself

effects.log: You paint the sky for the rite, badly, with love. {npc} says it is the finest thing ever painted, and means it. (+6 charm, +5 align)

events.text: On a jade platform over nothing at all you spar with {npc}, an immortal who fights like a fast river and laughs at every blow you land. You fight to a draw. {npc} demands a rematch at once, and another, and by sunset you have fought eleven times.
events.arc: The Rival on the Jade Platform

ok.log: You win the twelfth, just. {npc} sits down on the jade, laughing, and says you must do this every year. (+20 fame, +3 charm)

fail.log: {npc} wins the twelfth, and helps you up, and says you must do this every year. (-8 health, +3 charm)

choices.text: Call it a draw and share a meal

effects.log: You share a meal on the edge of the platform. {npc} eats like a soldier and talks like a poet. (+4 charm)
You bow and leave. {npc} shouts after you that a draw is not an ending. (+2 Mind)

events.text: A century of yearly duels with {npc} has turned into something neither of you can name. This year {he} does not draw {his} weapon. {He} only stands on the jade platform and says, "I am tired of fighting you. I am not tired of you."
events.arc: The Rival on the Jade Platform

effects.log: You lower it. You stand on the platform together and watch the clouds go under, saying nothing, for a whole day. (+5 charm, +4 align)
{npc} laughs, and you fight one more, the best of all, and at the end neither of you is trying to win. (+5 charm, +3 Mind)

events.text: {npc} has been challenged by a Demon General to a duel to the end, an old feud from before you met. {He} has not told you. You hear it from a crane.
events.arc: The Rival on the Jade Platform

ok.log: You win, and the Demon General goes home alive and thoughtful. {npc} is furious with you for a year, and then not at all. (+6 align, +40 fame)

fail.log: You lose, and live, and the General, impressed, calls off the feud anyway. {npc} nurses you back with very bad soup. (-20 health, +5 charm)

effects.log: You stand behind {npc}. {He} fights better knowing it, and wins, and turns to you before the dust has settled. (+5 charm, +3 align)

events.text: On the jade platform where you first fought, {npc} lays {his} weapon down beside yours, crossed, the old sign of a sworn bond. {He} asks for the rite of Dao companions, here, with the clouds going under.
events.arc: The Rival on the Jade Platform

choices.text: Take the rite on the platform

effects.log: You take the rite on the jade over nothing. Your old opponents come to watch and are very moved, and then demand a duel. (+6 charm, +300 years of life)

choices.text: Take the rite, and duel once more after

effects.log: You take the rite and then the best duel of your lives, and call it a draw forever. (+6 charm, +30 fame)

events.text: You come back from a hard year hurt, and the Nine Clouds Palace sends a healer: {npc}, who is brisk and kind and has cold hands, and tells you, with great seriousness, that you are a very bad patient.
events.arc: The Healer of the Nine Clouds

effects.log: You lie still and drink everything. {npc} is so surprised that {he} stays an extra week to make sure. (+10 health, +3 charm)
You argue about every pill. {npc} argues back. You are both enjoying it far too much. (+5 health, +4 charm)
You send {npc} away. You heal slowly, and badly, and think about cold hands. (+2 Mind)

events.text: {npc} comes to your isle now without being sent, with a basket of herbs and an excuse. Today there is no excuse. {He} sits on your step and says {he} has been healing immortals for two thousand years and has never once been asked how {he} is.
events.arc: The Healer of the Nine Clouds

effects.log: You ask. {npc} talks until the stars come out, and then sits a while longer in the dark. (+5 charm, +4 align)
You make tea, badly. {npc} drinks all of it and tells you what you did wrong, and is happy. (+5 charm)

events.text: A fever of the qi has come up from the Demon Abyss and is moving through the Upper Realm. {npc} has gone to the worst of it, on the lowest clouds, and has not come back, and the last message says only: more hands.
events.arc: The Healer of the Nine Clouds

effects.log: You work beside {npc} for a year, carrying, boiling, holding. The fever breaks. {He} falls asleep on your shoulder in the middle of a sentence. (+8 align, -5 health)

ok.log: You trace it to a cracked seal on the Abyss and close it. The fever ends in a week. {npc} looks at you as if you had hung the moon. (+6 align, +30 fame)

fail.log: You do not find it, and go back to carrying water instead. {npc} is glad of you either way. (+4 align, -8 health)

events.text: The fever is over. {npc} comes to your isle with an empty basket, for once, and no excuse, and asks, very plainly, as {he} asks patients where it hurts, whether you would take the rite of Dao companions with {him}.
events.arc: The Healer of the Nine Clouds

effects.log: You say yes. You take the rite in the Nine Clouds herb garden, among the bitter roots. It is the sweetest day of a very long life. (+6 charm, +300 years of life)

choices.text: Say yes, and ask how {he} is

effects.log: {npc} laughs until {he} has to sit down, and says "Very well, now." You take the rite at dusk. (+6 charm, +5 align)

events.text: {npc}, a reader of the Star Sea Pavilion, stops you on a cloud road and says, quite calmly, that {he} read your face in the stars four thousand years ago, before you were born, and has been waiting to see if it was a good likeness.
events.arc: The Reader Who Saw You Coming

effects.log: {npc} looks at you for a long time. "Better," {he} says. (+4 charm)
"That you would ask that," {npc} says, "and that I would not tell you." You are charmed against your will. (+3 charm, +2 Mind)

choices.text: Say you do not believe in fate

effects.log: "Neither do I," says {npc}. "That is what makes it interesting." (+3 Mind)

events.text: {npc} has been reading the stars about the two of you, and will not say what they say. You find out anyway: {he} has burned every chart. {He} wants, {he} says, for once in a long life, not to know how something ends.
events.arc: The Reader Who Saw You Coming

effects.log: You burn the last chart together on the Pavilion roof. Neither of you knows what happens next. It is wonderful. (+5 charm, +3 luck)
You read it. You never tell {npc} what it said. You are kinder to {him} from then on, which {he} notices. (+4 Mind, +3 charm)

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion has found out that {npc} burned a chart, which is the one crime it punishes. {He} is to be cast out, and in the Upper Realm a reader cast out of the Pavilion is never read for again, by anyone, which means never hired, never trusted.
events.arc: The Reader Who Saw You Coming

effects.log: You go together to a drifting isle with no name. You read nothing. You have each other and a garden. (+6 align, +4 charm)

choices.text: Plead the case at the Pavilion

ok.log: You plead, and the Pavilion Master, who once burned a chart too, quietly lets {npc} off. (+5 charm, +20 fame)

fail.log: The Master will not hear it. {npc} is cast out. You go with {him}. (+5 align)

events.text: Under a sky that neither of you has read, {npc} asks you for the rite of Dao companions. "I do not know if it will last," {he} says. "That is the point."
events.arc: The Reader Who Saw You Coming

effects.log: You take the rite under unread stars. Somewhere a reader of the Star Sea looks up and, for once, does not write anything down. (+6 charm, +300 years of life)
{npc} laughs. "Do not tell me," {he} says. You take the rite, and do not tell, and it does. (+6 charm, +4 luck)

events.text: Every dawn, on the far side of the cloud border, a general of the Demon Realm walks the wall: {npc}, in black armour, alone. Every dawn {he} stops at the same place and looks across. Today {he} lifts a hand.

effects.log: You lift a hand. The next dawn {npc} is there again, and so are you. (+3 charm)
You cross, which nobody does. {npc} is so surprised {he} forgets to draw a weapon, and you talk until noon. (+4 charm, +2 luck)
You turn away. The next dawn {npc} does not lift a hand, but is still there. (+1 Mind)

events.text: You and {npc} meet in secret, now, in the mist on the border, where neither realm can see. {He} tells you that the Demon Realm is planning a raid on your side in the spring. {He} is telling you because {he} would rather lose a raid than lose you.

effects.log: You warn them. The raid fails, without blood. {npc} is blamed, and demoted, and comes to the mist laughing. (+5 align, +3 charm)
You keep it, and on the night of the raid stand where the raiders will pass, and they turn back at the sight of you. Nobody is blamed. (+5 charm, +20 fame)

events.text: The secret is out. Both realms know about the mist on the border. The Demon Realm has ordered {npc} to bring your head. Your own side has ordered the same of you. {npc} is waiting in the mist, as always, unarmed.

effects.log: You go unarmed. You stand together in the mist while both realms watch, and neither army moves, because nobody knows what to do. (+8 align, +40 fame)

choices.text: Fight your way through both sides

ok.log: You cut a road through the mist and take {npc} away to a drifting isle, and both realms decide, at length, not to follow. (+5 charm, +30 fame)

fail.log: You get through, and {npc} carries you the last mile. (-25 health, +5 charm)

events.text: On a drifting isle that belongs to neither realm, {npc} takes off {his} black armour for the last time and sets it beside your own. {He} asks for the rite of Dao companions, with nobody's banner over it.

choices.text: Take the rite with no banner

effects.log: You take the rite on the isle of no realm. Both armies, watching from far off, lower their banners at the same moment, by accident, and pretend they did not. (+6 charm, +300 years of life)

choices.text: Sew the two banners into one

effects.log: You sew them together, badly, and hang it over the rite. In a thousand years it will be the flag of a truce. (+6 charm, +6 align)

events.text: At the edge of the Upper Realm, where the clouds end and the dark beyond begins, someone keeps a lantern lit so that nobody falls off: {npc}, who has done it alone for eleven thousand years, and is very glad, {he} says, of the company.
events.arc: The Lantern Keeper at the Edge

effects.log: You stay a month. {npc} shows you the stars beyond the edge, the ones nobody inside can see. (+4 Mind, +3 charm)

choices.text: Offer to keep the lantern a night

effects.log: You keep it a night while {npc} sleeps for the first time in a thousand years. {He} wakes and cannot stop smiling. (+4 align, +3 charm)
You leave. Looking back, you see the lantern swing once, like a wave. (+1 luck)

events.text: You come back to the edge every decade, then every year. {npc} has started keeping two cushions by the lantern. Today {he} tells you why {he} took the post: someone {he} loved fell off the edge, long ago, in the dark, and {he} has been holding up the lantern for them ever since.
events.arc: The Lantern Keeper at the Edge

effects.log: You hold it together. It burns brighter with two hands on it. (+5 charm, +4 align)

choices.text: Look over the edge for the lost one

effects.log: You look a long time. There is nothing but stars. {npc} thanks you for looking, which nobody else ever did. (+5 Mind, +4 charm)

events.text: A wind from beyond the edge has come, the kind that comes once in ten thousand years, and the lantern is guttering. If it goes out, nobody will find their way back along the edge for an age. {npc} is holding it with both hands and shaking.
events.arc: The Lantern Keeper at the Edge

choices.text: Shield the flame with your qi

ok.log: You stand between the lantern and the wind all night. At dawn the wind gives up. {npc} does not let go of your hand for a day. (+6 align, -10 health)

fail.log: The flame nearly goes; you give it your own warmth to keep it, and are cold for a century. {npc} keeps you warm. (-20 health, +5 charm)

choices.text: Light a second lantern from it

effects.log: You light a second from the first, and hold one each, and both survive. There are two lights at the edge now. (+5 Mind, +5 charm)

events.text: At the edge of everything, by the lantern, {npc} asks you for the rite of Dao companions. "I have kept a light for someone for eleven thousand years," {he} says. "I would like to keep one with someone."
events.arc: The Lantern Keeper at the Edge

choices.text: Take the rite by the lantern

effects.log: You take the rite at the edge of the heavens, with the dark on one side and the light on the other. The lantern has never burned so bright. (+6 charm, +300 years of life)

choices.text: Take the rite, and keep the lantern together

effects.log: You take the rite and the post together. Travellers at the edge tell of two keepers now, who argue, kindly, about the wick. (+6 charm, +5 align)

events.text: A minister of the Celestial Ministries, {npc}, has been writing you letters about policy. Long ones. Very dull ones, at first. Lately the letters have grown shorter and the policy has grown thin, and the last one is only about the weather on {his} isle, and how {he} thought of you.

effects.log: You write about the rain on your isle. {npc} answers within the hour. (+4 charm)
You write ten pages about grain. {npc} answers with eleven, and a pressed flower in the middle. (+3 Mind, +2 charm)
You stop. A letter comes once a year for a decade, then stops too. (+1 Mind)

events.text: You meet {npc} at last, at the Jade Court, in front of everyone. {He} is very correct, very formal, and drops {his} entire sheaf of papers when you bow.

effects.log: You pick them up together. Every one of them is a draft of a letter to you. Neither of you says anything. (+5 charm, +3 luck)
You pretend. {npc} is so grateful {he} writes you a letter about it that afternoon. (+4 charm, +2 Mind)

events.text: A rival minister has found your letters with {npc} and means to read them aloud before the whole Celestial Ministries, to shame {him} out of office.

effects.log: You stand at the Jade Court and read your own letters, every one. The Court is silent, then moved, then, mostly, envious. The rival withdraws. (+6 charm, +40 fame)

choices.text: Get the letters back before the hearing

ok.log: You take them back in the night, every page, and leave the rival a polite note. (+5 luck, +3 charm)

fail.log: You are caught with the letters in your hands, which is somehow worse. {npc} laughs until {he} cries. (+4 charm, -3 luck)

events.text: {npc} sends you one more letter. It is one line long, in {his} best hand: a request, in the old court form, for the rite of Dao companions.

effects.log: You write back one word. The rite is held at the Jade Court, and three ministers weep, and one of them is the rival. (+6 charm, +300 years of life)
You go to {his} isle and say it aloud, which nobody at the Court ever does. {npc} drops the papers again. (+6 charm, +4 align)

events.text: A young cultivator has climbed the white jade stairs, which takes a mortal life's whole strength, and collapsed at the top. {npc} is nineteen, ragged, stubborn, and carries a wooden token carved with your name. {He} says {he} is of your line, five generations down, and has come to see if the stories are true.

effects.log: {npc} laughs, and cries, and falls asleep on the stairs. You put your coat over {him}. (+5 align, +3 charm)
They say you fought a dragon, which you did not, and that you were kind to a beggar, which you did not know anyone saw. (+4 Mind)
You carry {npc} down to the foot of the stairs while {he} sleeps. {He} wakes below and thinks it was a dream. (+2 Mind, -2 align)

events.text: {npc}, the climber of your line, has been on your isle for a year. {He} cannot stay forever: a mortal cultivator up here ages strangely and fast. {He} must go back down, or begin, now, the long way up through the realms.

choices.text: Teach {him} for as long as {he} can stay

effects.log: You teach {npc} for three years, as hard as {he} can bear. {He} goes down stronger than anyone in five generations. (+5 align, +3 Mind)
You give {npc} a sprig of cloud-pine for the family shrine. Below, it grows into a tree that never sheds. (+4 align, +2 luck)

choices.text: Ask {him} to tell the family you are well

effects.log: {npc} promises, and goes down the white stairs, slowly, looking back at every landing. (+3 charm)

events.text: News comes up the stairs, a lifetime later: {npc}, the climber of your line, founded a school below, and taught in it until {he} was very old, and on {his} last day asked to be carried to the window that faces the mountain.

effects.log: You part the clouds. The school is still there, small and busy, and over the gate is your name, misspelled. (+6 align, +3 Mind)
A single cloud-pine blossom falls into the school's courtyard. Its students say it is lucky, and fight over it, kindly. (+4 align, +3 luck)

events.text: Incense smoke comes up through the clouds in a shape: a petition. It is from the sect you trained in below. They have burned nine thousand sticks of incense, all at once, to send it. A great sect is at their gate, and they ask whether the one who went up the mountain remembers them.

effects.log: You send down a single bolt of clear sky over their gate. The great sect at the gate goes home, thoughtfully. (+6 align, +30 fame)
The petition fades. Below, the old sect holds its gate alone, and holds it. You are proud and ashamed in equal parts. (+3 Mind, -3 align)

choices.text: Send down a dream to the sect head

effects.log: The sect head dreams of you, saying nothing, only standing at the gate. In the morning the sect head does the same. (+5 align, +2 Mind)

events.text: The old sect below has grown proud. Since your sign, they boast that the heavens fight for them, and they have started a war of their own with a smaller sect, sure you will help again. A second petition rises in the smoke.

effects.log: You let the smoke pass. The old sect loses the war, and learns, painfully, to stand on its own feet. (+5 Mind, +2 align)

choices.text: Send down a sign against them

effects.log: Rain falls on their war banners for a month. The war ends of embarrassment. (+5 align, +3 Mind)
You help. They win. They are a little worse for it, and so, somehow, are you. (-5 align, +20 fame)

events.text: The old sect below is gone. Not destroyed: merged, a century ago, with the rival that was at its gate, and the new sect has a name that is both their names together. In its hall there is a portrait. It is of you.

effects.log: You look until the clouds close. The portrait is not a good likeness. You love it anyway. (+5 Mind, +3 align)

choices.text: Send down a blessing on the new name

effects.log: You send down a good harvest and a talented generation. The new sect never knows. (+6 align)

events.text: Your spouse below has burned a letter, as the old custom says, so that it would rise, and the ash comes up through the clouds, settles in a cupped palm and becomes a letter again. It is not long. It says the plum tree you planted has fruited for the first time, and everyone is well, and the house is very quiet.

effects.log: The letter you burn goes down as warm rain on one roof. Your spouse stands in the courtyard in it, laughing. (+6 align, +4 charm)
You keep it in your sleeve. On the Jade Court's dullest days you read it again. (+4 Mind)
You part the clouds. There is the plum tree, and under it, very small, someone looking up. (+5 align)

events.text: Another letter rises in ash, years later. The handwriting is shakier. Your spouse writes that the plum tree has fruited every year now, and that they would like, before the end, one sign that you read the letters.

choices.text: Send a plum blossom in winter

effects.log: The plum tree below blooms in the snow, the week the letter was burned. Your spouse sits under it a whole afternoon. (+8 align, +3 charm)
You stand in their dream under the plum tree and say nothing, and that is the right thing. They wake smiling. (+6 align, +4 Mind)

events.text: A cultivator has climbed the white stairs to challenge you. {npc} is the grandchild of your oldest rival below, raised on stories of you, every one of them unflattering, and has spent {his} whole life getting strong enough to come up here and settle the family's account.

ok.log: You let {npc} fight until {he} is tired and then end it with one finger. {He} sits down on the jade and laughs, despite everything. (+3 charm, +2 align)

fail.log: You are careless. {npc} lands one blow, a real one, and is so astonished {he} forgets to land another. (-6 health, +4 charm)

effects.log: You tell {npc} the whole story, with your faults in it. {He} listens with clenched fists and leaves without a word. (+5 align, +3 Mind)
{npc} spits on the stairs and goes down, furious. You feel very old. (+2 Mind)

events.text: {npc}, your old rival's heir, has climbed the stairs again, ten years older. This time {he} is not here to fight. {His} grandparent, your old rival, is dying below, and asked {him} to carry one sentence up the mountain.

effects.log: "Tell them I was proud to lose to them," {npc} says, stiffly, and then breaks, and you sit together on the stairs. (+8 align, +4 charm)
You send back: "And I was afraid of you, every day." {npc} carries it down, and your old rival dies laughing. (+8 align, +3 Mind)

events.text: Through a gap in the clouds you see it: a temple, in a valley below, with a statue in it. The statue is of you, more or less: too tall, wrong robes, holding a fish for reasons you cannot imagine. Mortals are bringing it rice.

effects.log: You watch for a year. A widow with a sick son, a boy who wants to be strong, an old man who just likes the quiet. (+4 Mind, +3 align)
You answer the widow's. The son recovers. The temple doubles in size by spring. (+6 align, +20 fame)
You close them. Some honours are too strange to look at for long. (+2 Mind)

events.text: The temple has grown. There are monks now, and rules, and a tax on candles, and a head monk who says that you have commanded certain things. You did not command any of them. Several are unkind.

choices.text: Send a sign against the head monk

effects.log: A gust of wind blows every false rule off the temple wall. The monks argue about it for a century and come out kinder. (+6 align, +3 Mind)
You let them. The temple splits into two temples, and both are better than the one. (+4 Mind)
The statue opens its mouth and says: "Be kind. And the fish was never mine." The valley is never the same. (+8 align, +40 fame)

events.text: A column of imperial incense, yellow as a dragon robe, climbs through the clouds to your isle: an emperor below has heard of you, and asks the immortal who went up the mountain to bless the dynasty for ten thousand years.

effects.log: You bless it, lightly. The dynasty lasts four hundred years, which is ten thousand in imperial arithmetic. (+20 fame, +2 luck)
You send the blessing past the palace and into the fields. The harvests are very good for a century, and the emperor takes the credit. (+6 align)
The incense falls back on the palace as a fine yellow dust. The court astrologers spend a decade arguing what it means. (+3 Mind)

events.text: The dynasty you blessed has decided it can do no wrong. Its armies march under a banner with your name on it, and its tax collectors say heaven sent them. A second column of incense rises, thanking you.

effects.log: You withdraw it, very publicly: the banner with your name tears in a clear sky in front of the whole army. The army goes home. (+8 align, +20 fame)

choices.text: Send a dream to the emperor
