effects.log: The emperor dreams of you weighing the empire on a scale against one hungry child. The tax is halved in the morning. (+6 align, +3 Mind)
The empire goes on under your name. Nobody asks you whether you like it. (-4 align, +2 luck)

events.text: Through the clouds you see two armies in a valley below, drawn up for a battle that will start at dawn. You can count them: twelve thousand on one side, nine on the other. From up here you could end it with a gesture, or with a word, or not at all.

effects.log: Fog fills the valley at dawn. Neither army can find the other. By noon both generals have lost their nerve. (+8 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Do nothing; it is their world now

effects.log: You watch. It is a short battle and a long grief. You do not look away. (+5 Mind, -3 align)

choices.text: Send a dream to both generals

effects.log: Both dream the same dream of the same grave. In the morning they meet in the middle of the valley, unarmed, and talk. (+6 align, +4 Mind)

events.text: The war you stopped with fog has come back, a generation later, in a different valley. The grandchildren of the two generals have learned that heaven sometimes intervenes, and have started to wait for it. Both armies are praying to you by name.

choices.text: Stay out of it this time

effects.log: You stay out. The armies wait three days for a sign, and when none comes, march home in confusion. Nobody fights. (+5 Mind, +3 align)
The fog comes. The war ends again. You wonder whether you are teaching them anything at all. (+4 align, +2 luck)
You write one word in the clouds over both armies: "Yourselves." It is argued about for three hundred years. (+5 Mind, +30 fame)

events.text: A mortal has climbed the white jade stairs: an ordinary thief, with no cultivation at all, who climbed for nine years on stubbornness alone to steal a single peach of immortality. You catch {npc} in your orchard with the peach halfway to {his} mouth.
events.arc: The Mortal Who Climbed the Stairs

effects.log: {npc} eats it. Nothing happens, for a while. Then {he} sits down and cries, for reasons {he} cannot explain. (+5 align, +3 charm)
{npc} gives it back without a fight, and asks only if {he} may sit and look at the clouds before going down. (+3 Mind)
"My mother is dying," {npc} says. It is not true. Then {he} tells you the true reason, which is much stranger. (+4 Mind)

events.text: {npc}, the thief who climbed the white stairs, has not gone back down. {He} has become a kind of servant in the Upper Realm, the only mortal here, sweeping courtyards for immortals who never noticed {him}. Today the Celestial Ministries have noticed {him}, and wants {him} removed.
events.arc: The Mortal Who Climbed the Stairs

effects.log: You speak for {npc} at the Court. The ministers are bewildered that anyone cares, and leave {him} be. (+6 align, +3 charm)
You start {npc} on the first breath of the first method. {He} will die long before the second realm, and does not mind. (+5 align, +4 Mind)
You walk {npc} down, all the way, a mortal's pace. At the bottom {he} turns and bows, and goes into the world very straight-backed. (+4 align, +2 luck)

events.text: The village where you were born is going under water. Through the clouds you see the dam: a great work of the empire below, a lake that will feed a province. The village has a month. Its people are packing carts, and some of them are looking up.

effects.log: You let it come. You watch your first roof go under, and the province below grows green for a thousand years. (+5 Mind, +3 align)

choices.text: Raise the village on a hill

effects.log: You lift the village, house by house, onto the hill above the lake, one night. The engineers below go mad trying to explain it. (+6 align, +30 fame)
You lift the old well out of the water and set it on the shore. Somebody plants a willow by it. (+4 align, +3 Mind)

events.text: Under the lake where your village was, the mortals below say, a light can be seen on still nights: a window that never went dark. Fishermen row out to look at it. They say it is the immortal's old house, keeping a lamp lit.

effects.log: You light it, faint and gold, under the water. The fishermen sing on the lake at night now. (+5 align, +4 charm)

choices.text: Let the story be a story

effects.log: You let it be. The light they see is the moon, and the story is better than the truth. (+4 Mind)

events.text: A novel has been written about you in the world below. You know because somebody burned a copy as an offering and the ash drifted up to your isle. It is nine hundred pages long. In it you are taller, crueler, have three swords and a talking horse, and your great love is someone you never met.

effects.log: You read all nine hundred pages. It is terrible. You cannot put it down. (+4 Mind, +3 charm)

choices.text: Burn the ash a second time

effects.log: You burn it again. There is no third ash. The novel, below, goes into its eleventh printing. (+2 Mind)
The author dreams of you, reading, and frowning at chapter forty. The second edition fixes chapter forty. (+5 charm, +20 fame)

events.text: The novel about you has a sequel. In the sequel you ascend to the heavens and become a goddess of rivers, which is two things you are not. Immortals at the Jade Court have started reading it, and quoting it, and calling you by the horse's name.

effects.log: You answer to the horse's name for a century. The Jade Court finds you suddenly much more approachable. (+5 charm, +20 fame)

choices.text: Write a correction and burn it down

effects.log: You write the true story, very plainly, and burn it down. It sells badly below, and is loved by twelve readers, deeply. (+5 Mind, +3 align)

events.text: You have walked to the edge of the heavens. Here the clouds stop the way a coast stops, and beyond them there is nothing, not dark, not void: an absence that makes your eyes slide away. Somebody has built a bench here, facing outward. It is very old.

effects.log: You sit and look at nothing for a year. You come back changed in a way you cannot name. (+8 Mind)

choices.text: Throw a stone over the edge

effects.log: The stone goes out and does not fall and does not stop. You feel it going for a decade. (+4 Mind, +2 luck)
You turn back. Some edges are for knowing about. (+3 align)

events.text: You have come back to the bench at the edge of the heavens, and today someone else is sitting on it: an immortal so old their robes are a fashion of the First Heaven, who says they built the bench, and that the edge is moving. Inward. A span every ten thousand years.

effects.log: "The end of this heaven," the old one says, "or the start of the next. Nobody has gone to see." (+5 Mind)
"Nothing," the old one says. "Or everything. Sit with me and we will think." You sit. (+5 Mind, +3 align)

events.text: The old bench-builder has gone over the edge. They left a note on the bench, held down by the stone you threw years ago, which came back: "It is not the end. It is a door, and it needs someone on this side to hold it. Will you?"

effects.log: You sit on the bench at the edge of the heavens for a hundred years, holding a door you cannot see. The edge stops moving. Nobody inside ever knows. (+10 Mind, +8 align)

ok.log: You go a little way into the next heaven and see it: young, unfinished, full of light. You come back, because someone has to tell this one. (+12 Mind, +80 fame)

fail.log: The door throws you back onto the bench, very gently, like a parent putting a child to bed. Not yet. (-15 health, +5 Mind)

choices.text: Leave the note for the next to come

effects.log: You leave it. Someone else will hold the door. You go home and plant a tree, which is also a way of holding one. (+4 align, +3 luck)

events.text: One of the stars that the world below steers by is dying. The Star Sea Pavilion has seen it; the Celestial Ministries have filed it; nobody has done anything. In three hundred years it will go out, and sailors below will lose their way, and the calendar will fail, and the planting with it.

effects.log: The Court forms a ministry, which forms a committee, which meets every century. (+2 Mind, +20 fame)
It takes ten years to fly there. Up close it is old, and tired, and very hot. (+5 Mind, -8 health)

choices.text: Teach the world below new stars

effects.log: You send down dreams to a thousand navigators of a different star to steer by. In three hundred years nobody will notice the old one go. (+6 align, +4 Mind)

events.text: Up close, the dying star can be talked to, in the way a forge can be talked to. It does not want to go out. It is only very tired. It could be kept burning, if something gave it fire.

ok.log: You pour yourself into it for a decade, and it brightens, and will burn another ten thousand years. Sailors below never know. (+10 align, -20 health)

fail.log: It takes more than you have. It brightens a little and you have to stop. It will burn a thousand years longer, which is something. (+5 align, -25 health)

effects.log: You sit with it until it is calm. When it goes, three hundred years later, it goes softly, and the sailors below see a last beautiful light. (+6 Mind, +4 align)

choices.text: Bring the Nine Clouds Palace to feed it

effects.log: The alchemists come, grumbling, with furnace-fire, and feed the star for a century. It is the greatest thing the palace ever does. (+6 align, +40 fame)

events.text: The sea of clouds has thinned, once in an age, and beneath it, where there should be only sky, you see roofs: a city, vast, white stone and green bronze, hanging under the Upper Realm like a reflection. Nobody you ask has ever heard of it.

effects.log: You go down through the thinning clouds. The city's gate is open. There is dust on everything, a hundred thousand years deep. (+5 Mind)

choices.text: Map it from above before the clouds close

effects.log: You map it for nine days. Then the clouds close, and you have the only map of a city nobody knows. (+4 Mind, +2 luck)
The Court does not believe you, and then the clouds close, and it is too late to prove it. (+2 Mind)

events.text: The city under the clouds had a name, written over every door, in a script that is almost the script of the world below. Its people were mortals who learned to live in the sky, before the immortals came. The immortals, it seems, did not want neighbours.

effects.log: The last record is a decree, sealed with a seal you have seen at the Celestial Ministries. You go home very quiet. (+6 Mind, -2 luck)

choices.text: Leave an offering for the dead

effects.log: You leave incense in the city square. The smoke rises straight, as if somebody were still breathing it. (+5 align)
You take a bronze bell from a temple. It does not ring for anyone but you. (+3 luck, +2 Mind)

events.text: You have the Celestial Ministries' seal on the decree that ended the city under the clouds. The Court does not know you know. A minister you trust tells you, quietly, that some truths are kept by the Court because the Court could not survive them.

effects.log: You read the decree at the Jade Court. There is a silence that lasts a century. Then the Court builds a memorial, and an archive, and is changed. (+10 align, +60 fame)

choices.text: Keep it, and remember them yourself

effects.log: You keep the city's name. Once a year you go to where it lies under the clouds and say it aloud. (+6 Mind, +4 align)

choices.text: Give it to the Demon Realm

effects.log: The Demon Realm uses it as it uses everything. The Court is shaken for a thousand years. (+20 fame, -8 align)

events.text: On a floating isle two immortals have been playing one game of go for ten thousand years. One of them stood up this morning, said "I must stretch my legs," and has not come back. The other looks at you and taps the empty seat.
events.arc: The Game of Ten Thousand Years

effects.log: You sit. The board is so deep in its game that each stone you lay takes a year to understand. (+6 Mind)

choices.text: Go and find the missing player

effects.log: You find them at the bottom of the isle, stretching, and three thousand years behind on the news. (+3 charm, +2 Mind)
You look at it for a day. In it, you are almost sure, is the history of the world below. (+4 Mind)

events.text: You have played the ten-thousand-year game for a century, and you have realised: every stone on the board is a kingdom below. The game is the world. Your next move will drown a coast or save it.
events.arc: The Game of Ten Thousand Years

choices.text: Play the move that saves the coast

effects.log: You play it. The other player smiles. Below, a sea wall holds in a storm nobody expected it to survive. (+8 align, +4 Mind)
You stand up. The other player sighs and waits for someone else. Below, nothing changes for a while. (+4 Mind)

choices.text: Ask the other player who is winning

effects.log: "The game," says the other player. You find that is the only true answer. (+6 Mind)

events.text: The other player in the game of ten thousand years has stood up at last, for the first time since before you were born, and says: "It is yours now. I am tired of the world." And leaves.
events.arc: The Game of Ten Thousand Years

effects.log: You play on, alone, for centuries. Below, the world is a little gentler than it would have been. You will never tell anyone why. (+10 align, +6 Mind)

choices.text: Sweep the stones into the box

effects.log: You sweep the board clear. Below, nothing ends; the world simply goes on without a game. It is, you decide, better so. (+8 Mind)
You find a young immortal with good hands and a kind heart, and teach the rules. You play together for ten thousand years. (+6 align, +4 charm)

events.text: A mountain in the Upper Realm has opened its eyes. It is not a mountain: it is an immortal of the First Heaven who sat down to meditate before this heaven rose and has been sitting ever since. It is waking. It is very large, and very confused.

effects.log: You speak to it in the oldest language you know. It answers in an older one. You begin, slowly, to understand each other. (+6 Mind)
Every faction musters on the clouds around the waking mountain. It looks at them all and is frightened. (-2 align)
You sing an old lullaby from below. The mountain sighs and closes its eyes for another age. (+5 align, +3 charm)

events.text: The sleeper of the First Heaven wants to know where everyone went. You are the one who has to tell it: its heaven fell, its people are gone, and the world it fell asleep in is a story in the Ruins.

effects.log: It weeps, and the weeping is a rain that lasts a decade over the whole Upper Realm. Afterwards, it asks to learn this heaven. (+8 align, +4 Mind)

choices.text: Take it to the Ruins of the First Heaven

effects.log: You walk with it to the Ruins, which takes a century. It stands in its old city and is quiet a long time, and then thanks you. (+8 Mind, +40 fame)

events.text: The factions have surrounded the waking sleeper with armies, and the sleeper, frightened, has stood up. When it stands, isles tilt. A Star Marshal is about to give the order to strike.

choices.text: Stand between the army and the sleeper

ok.log: You stand there until both sides are calm enough to listen. The sleeper sits down again, carefully, and the order is never given. (+10 align, +60 fame)

fail.log: The order is given. You take the first strike for the sleeper, and the shock of that stops everyone. (-30 health, +8 align)

effects.log: You climb its shoulder and talk into its ear for a day. It sits. The armies, embarrassed, go home. (+8 align, +4 Mind)

events.text: There is a crack in the sky above the sky. Only an Immortal Sovereign can see it: a hairline of darkness across the highest heaven, longer every century. Through it, at night, something like wind comes in. The other Sovereigns will not speak of it.

effects.log: You study it a century. It is not a wound. It is a seam, where this heaven was stitched to something else, and the stitches are wearing through. (+8 Mind)

choices.text: Raise it with the other Sovereigns

effects.log: The Sovereigns go silent at once, which tells you more than any answer. One of them comes to you that night. (+5 Mind)
You leave it. Every night you look up and it is a little longer. (+2 luck, -2 Mind)

events.text: An old Sovereign tells you the truth, at night, at the top of the heavens: the seam has been mended before, three times, each time by a Sovereign who stitched it with their own life and became the thread. The stitches are wearing through again.

choices.text: Offer to be the next stitch

effects.log: The old Sovereign looks at you a long time, then says: "Not yet. But I will remember you said it." (+10 align, +6 Mind)

choices.text: Find another way to mend it

ok.log: You find it: a seam can be sewn by many hands, each giving a little. It will take every immortal in the heavens a year of qi. It can be done. (+10 Mind, +80 fame)

fail.log: You find nothing better. But you know now what the price will be, and that someone will have to pay it. (+6 Mind)

effects.log: You keep the secret, as the old Sovereigns have. It weighs exactly as much as the sky. (+5 Mind, -3 charm)

events.text: The seam in the highest heaven is mending itself, very slowly, and you understand why: the old Sovereign who told you the truth has gone up to it, alone, without telling you. You can see them, a thin bright thread along the dark, stitching.

choices.text: Go up and stitch beside them

effects.log: You sew beside them a hundred years and then they let you go, and sew on alone, and the seam closes. You keep their name. (+12 align, +8 Mind)
You sit beneath the seam until it closes. It takes a thousand years. You do not leave once. (+8 Mind, +6 align)

events.text: The sea of clouds is lower this century. You notice it on your own isle first: the cloud-line on the rocks, a finger's width below where it was. Then the Star Sea Pavilion publishes it, and then the panic starts. If the sea of clouds drains, the Upper Realm will rest on nothing.
events.arc: The Sinking of the Sea of Clouds

choices.text: Find where it is draining to

effects.log: You follow the slope of the clouds for a decade, downward, to a whirlpool of vapour the size of a province. (+5 Mind)

choices.text: Calm the panic at the Jade Court

effects.log: You stand up at the Jade Court and say what you know, plainly. The panic slows. (+20 fame, +3 charm)
You anchor your isle with chains of qi and wait. Your neighbours start anchoring theirs to yours. (+3 luck, +2 align)

events.text: At the bottom of the whirlpool in the sea of clouds, there is a hole in the heavens, and through it the clouds are pouring down into the world below as rain: a great rain, nine years long, over the driest desert there is. Below, the desert is turning green.
events.arc: The Sinking of the Sea of Clouds

ok.log: You close it. The sea of clouds stops sinking. Below, the rain stops, and the new green in the desert holds, mostly. (+6 Mind, +60 fame)

fail.log: You close it halfway. The clouds sink slower; the desert gets half its rain. Everyone is half grateful. (-20 health, +4 align)

choices.text: Leave it open for nine more years

effects.log: You hold the panic above at bay for nine years while the desert below drinks. Then you close it. A new country is born down there. (+10 align, +4 Mind)

choices.text: Fetch the Nine Clouds Palace to seal it

effects.log: The array masters come, and argue, and seal it in a week, beautifully. They take the credit. (+4 align, +3 Mind)

events.text: Behind a waterfall on a drifting isle is a door, and behind the door an archive: shelf upon shelf of glass spheres, each with a tiny world inside, turning. A label in old script: "The worlds below that came before the world below." There are thousands.

effects.log: Inside is a whole world, smaller than a pea: forests, cities, wars, a child flying a kite. You watch until it is dawn in there. (+6 Mind)
The keeper is a moth the size of a hand, with ink on its wings, very glad to have a visitor. (+4 Mind, +2 charm)
You close it. Some things are better left on the shelf. (+3 align)

events.text: There is an empty space on the archive's last shelf, with a new label, freshly written in the old script: the name of the world below, your world, the one you came up from.

choices.text: Ask the keeper what it means

effects.log: The moth explains, with great embarrassment, that the space is only a reservation, and that worlds can stay unshelved forever if someone up here is looking after them. (+6 Mind, +4 align)
You scratch it out. The moth weeps ink, and then, a little, agrees with you. (+5 align, +2 luck)

choices.text: Leave it, and go home very quiet

effects.log: You go home and look down at the world below for a long time, and it looks back. (+5 Mind)

events.text: You have been looking after the world below, quietly, for a long time now: a word here, a rain there. The archive's keeper comes to your isle on its inky wings to say that the reserved space on the last shelf has been taken down. Nobody needs it now.

effects.log: The moth bows and gives you the label, which you hang above your door. (+6 align, +100 years of life)

choices.text: Ask to see the oldest world

effects.log: The moth shows you the first sphere on the first shelf. Inside, it is morning, and someone like you is looking up. (+8 Mind)

events.text: A second moon has risen over the Upper Realm. It is jade-coloured, smaller than the first, and it rose without any warning from behind the edge of the heavens. The tides of the sea of clouds have gone strange. Every faction is sending someone to look.

effects.log: You fly a year to reach it. It is hollow, and inside it is a garden, and the garden is singing. (+6 Mind)
You watch it cross the sky a hundred nights. On the hundred and first it pauses over your isle, as if it knows you. (+4 Mind, +2 luck)

choices.text: Go to the Star Sea Pavilion

effects.log: The Pavilion is in chaos: the second moon is in none of its charts, past or future. (+3 Mind, +20 fame)

events.text: Inside the jade moon's singing garden, you find its gardener: an immortal from a heaven next to this one, whose heaven ended. They put what was left of it in a moon and steered it here. They would like to stay, if the heaven will have them.

choices.text: Speak for them at the Celestial Ministries

effects.log: You speak for a stranger heaven at the Court for a century. In the end the second moon is given a place in the sky and a seat at the Jade Court. (+10 align, +60 fame)
You help steer it behind the first moon, where nobody looks. It is the Upper Realm's best-kept secret. (+6 align, +4 luck)

choices.text: Tell them the heavens are full

effects.log: The gardener bows, and steers the jade moon away into the dark. You watch it go for a year. (+4 Mind, -6 align)

events.text: The jade moon has been part of the sky for a century now. Its gardener has sent you the first fruit of its garden: a peach that tastes of a heaven you will never see, and a note that says the moon's people are learning your heaven's songs.

effects.log: It tastes of a whole other heaven's evenings. You will dream of them for the rest of your life. (+200 years of life, +4 Mind)
You plant it on your isle. In a thousand years there is an orchard of another heaven's peaches, and people come from everywhere to sit in it. (+6 align, +40 fame)

events.text: An old immortal you respect has taken a vow of silence for a hundred years, to hear what the heavens say when no one is talking. They have asked you to take it with them. It is a great honour, and a hundred years is long, even here.

effects.log: You fall silent. For the first year it is unbearable. For the second, merely very hard. (+5 Mind)
You decline. The old immortal nods and does not answer, already silent. (+2 Mind)

choices.text: Take it for one year only

effects.log: You keep a year of silence, and hear the clouds moving, and are glad, and talk again. (+4 Mind, +2 align)

events.text: Fifty years into your vow of silence, you hear it: under everything, very faint, the heavens are humming one note, the same note, always. It is the note a bell makes long after it has been struck. Somebody, once, struck the heavens.

effects.log: You keep listening. By the eightieth year you can hear the shape of the hand that struck it. (+8 Mind)

choices.text: Break the vow to tell someone

effects.log: You speak, and the note is gone, and you are never sure afterwards that you heard it. (+3 Mind, -2 luck)

events.text: The hundred years end. The old immortal who took the vow with you speaks first, and says only: "Did you hear it?" You did. Neither of you has to say what it was. The question now is what to do with it.

effects.log: You ring the heavens once, with the side of your hand, softly. Every immortal in the Upper Realm stops what they are doing and listens, for one breath. (+10 Mind, +60 fame)

choices.text: Keep it to the two of you

effects.log: You keep it. Every few centuries you and the old immortal sit together and say nothing at all, and listen. (+8 Mind, +4 charm)

events.text: An immortal arrives at the gate of your isle and asks to be taken in as a disciple. You know the face. A thousand years ago, below, in the world you came up from, this immortal was the one who taught you your first stance.

effects.log: You take your old teacher in as a disciple, and teach them, and they are the most difficult student you have ever had. (+5 prestige, +4 charm)

choices.text: Offer them a seat as an elder

effects.log: They refuse. "I came to learn," they say. "Teach." (+3 prestige, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Send them to a better teacher

effects.log: They go, and write to you later that the better teacher was not better. (+2 Mind)

events.text: Your old teacher, now your disciple, comes to you after a decade and corrects your stance, the first stance, the one they taught you a thousand years ago. You have been doing it slightly wrong all this time.

effects.log: You correct it. Something that was crooked in your whole art straightens. You are both very pleased. (+6 Mind, +4 prestige)

choices.text: Show them why you changed it

effects.log: You show them. They watch, and then they laugh and say, "Good. You learned the thing I could not teach." (+6 Mind, +4 align)

events.text: Centuries pass below. The valley of your temple has been through two wars and a flood, and the temple has fallen, and been rebuilt, and fallen. What is left is the statue, too tall, holding its fish, in a field. A child sweeps the leaves off its feet every morning, unasked.

choices.text: Send the child a good year

effects.log: The child's family has the best harvest in the valley that year, and the child goes on sweeping, as if it were a job. (+5 align, +2 luck)

choices.text: Let the statue crumble at last

effects.log: You let the rain have it. The child plants a tree where it stood, and the valley calls it your tree. (+4 Mind, +3 align)
You watch the child sweep until the clouds close. You do not know the child's name. It does not matter. (+5 Mind)

events.text: The record of the Debate of the Thousand Daos is copied out in a hundred hands and, by some accident, a page of it drifts down through the clouds and lands in the world below, in the courtyard of a village school. The schoolteacher reads your words aloud.
events.arc: The Debate of the Thousand Daos

effects.log: You listen through the clouds as the children argue about your words, loudly, and get most of it wrong, and one thing right that you had missed. (+6 Mind)
You let the next page fall. The school becomes, in a hundred years, the most argumentative academy in the empire. (+5 align, +20 fame)

events.text: A lightning-flower from your crater has gone over the edge of the clouds on the wind and taken root below, on a hill where farmers are afraid of storms. It crackles at night. The farmers have started to gather round it when thunder comes, and are less afraid.

choices.text: Send down a gentle storm to feed it

effects.log: A soft storm comes, and the flower drinks it, and a dozen more come up around it. The hill is a garden by spring. (+6 align, +2 luck)
The farmers tend it as well as anyone up here could, and name it after the sky. (+5 Mind)

events.text: The dynasty you once blessed has ended, as all of them do. The last column of yellow incense from its palace is thin, and carries not a request but an apology, written by its last emperor, a scholar who never wanted the throne.

effects.log: You let the incense settle on your isle. Below, the last emperor retires to a farm and lives, for once, without anyone praying to them. (+6 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Send a blessing to the scholar, not the throne

effects.log: The scholar's little farm has very good rain for the rest of a long, quiet life. (+5 align, +2 luck)

events.text: The ash that rises from the world below this year is not a letter. It is a single pressed plum blossom, from the tree you planted, with no words at all.

effects.log: You keep it between the pages of the letters. It never quite loses its scent. (+5 Mind, +3 charm)
A plum blossom falls into a courtyard below, out of season, out of a clear sky. Somebody there picks it up and laughs. (+6 align)

events.text: The novel about you has become a play below, and the play has become a festival, and once a year a whole city dresses as you, three swords and a horse each, and parades. A burned playbill drifts up through the clouds.

effects.log: You watch the whole parade from above. Ten thousand of you, all wrong, all laughing. It is the best day of the century. (+6 charm, +3 align)
A white cloud-horse appears in the parade for one hour and then is gone. The festival is twice as big the next year. (+5 charm, +30 fame)

events.text: {npc}, your old rival's heir, has become a sect head below. The first thing {he} did in the seat was burn incense to you, both families' incense, side by side. The smoke comes up through the clouds twisted together.

effects.log: You let the twisted smoke settle on your isle. Below, two families who hated each other for a century share a festival. (+8 align, +3 charm)
You write "Enough" in the clouds over the sect. {npc} reads it, and smiles, and has it carved over the gate. (+6 align, +3 Mind)

events.text: {npc}, the thief who climbed the white stairs, is old now. Below, or above, wherever {he} ended up, {he} has been telling the story of the immortal's orchard to anyone who will listen. It has become the most famous story in a whole province.
events.arc: The Mortal Who Climbed the Stairs

effects.log: In a dream you stand at the back of a crowded room in the world below and hear {npc} tell it. You are much nicer in the story. (+5 charm, +4 align)
A peach appears on {npc}'s table one morning. {He} does not eat it. {He} sets it on the windowsill and looks at it until {he} dies, very happy, many years later. (+6 align, +2 luck)

events.text: Once a year the people of the lake that drowned your village row out to the middle with paper lanterns, and set them on the water above where the old houses are, and say the names of the families who lived there. Yours is one of the names.

effects.log: You hear it, said by a stranger, kindly, on the water. You did not know how much you needed that. (+6 Mind, +3 align)
All the lanterns brighten at once. The lake festival is the brightest in its history, and nobody knows why. (+6 align, +20 fame)

events.text: A third generation in the valley of the fog. They have stopped waiting for heaven. They have built, on the field where the armies were to meet, a fair. Both sides come to it. The fog, when it comes now, is only weather.

choices.text: Send a real fog, for old times

effects.log: A thick, friendly fog rolls over the fair. Everyone laughs and buys hot soup. (+5 align, +3 charm)
You let them be. That was what you wanted all along. (+6 Mind)

events.text: Your echo from the Abyss is gone, but sometimes, when you are about to do something unkind, you hear it: your own voice, a moment early, saying the unkind thing. It is very useful. You stop, every time.

effects.log: You thank the echo aloud on a quiet isle. For a moment you hear it laugh, in your voice, and then nothing at all. (+6 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Teach it to say the kind thing

effects.log: It takes a century. Now, sometimes, your echo says the kind thing a moment early, and you only have to agree. (+6 Mind, +4 charm)

events.text: The mountain you sat into being has become a place. Immortals live on its slopes now, and a small sect, and a cloud-tea garden, and a shrine on the peak to whoever sat here first. The shrine has no name on it.

effects.log: You write it small. Visitors who know touch it on the way past, for luck. (+30 fame, +2 luck)
You leave it. A mountain does not need a name to be a mountain. (+6 Mind, +3 align)

events.text: The Dao Lord who became the Dao left the light changed, and it has stayed changed. Some days you catch, in the slant of it over your isle, a doorway with someone sitting in it. It is only the light. You make tea anyway.

effects.log: You pour two. One is always empty by evening, though you never see it drunk. (+6 Mind, +3 align)
You sit in your own doorway, waiting for nobody in particular. A young immortal passing by stops, and asks you something. (+5 Mind, +4 charm)

events.text: {npc}, who found the Dao of Waiting, has disciples now: eleven very patient immortals who sit on {his} isle and do almost nothing, beautifully. {He} would like you to come and see whether they are doing it right.

effects.log: You sit with them a whole year. At the end of it you are the least patient person on the isle, and the happiest. (+6 Mind, +3 charm)
You send a sandglass that runs for a hundred years. {npc} writes back that it is far too fast. (+4 charm, +3 Mind)

events.text: The young immortal whose tribulation came down while your storm watched has grown strong, and has come to find you. The thunder follows {npc} too, now, a small storm of {his} own. The two storms circle each other overhead like dogs.

effects.log: The two storms play over your isle for a day, and the rain is warm, and the young immortal laughs and laughs. (+5 charm, +3 luck)
You teach {npc} to call the storm and send it away. {He} learns faster than you did. (+5 Mind, +4 align)

events.text: {npc} of the Earth Dao has come to live on the bank of your river, in a stone house, and argues with you every evening and has, without admitting it, started letting the river run through {his} garden.

effects.log: You never mention it. The garden is the greenest on the isle. {npc} grows very fond of you, silently, like a stone warming. (+5 charm, +4 Mind)
{npc} goes red and says it is a drainage arrangement. You both laugh until the river laughs too. (+5 charm, +3 align)

events.text: The one in the grey robe who asked the question at your lecture comes to your isle, alone, a century later. They take off the hood. You have seen the face before: on the oldest statue in the Celestial Ministries, the one with no name under it.

effects.log: You bow. The one in grey bows back, and sits in your hall for a day listening to your disciples train, and goes. Your isle is never quite ordinary again. (+10 prestige, +5 Mind)

choices.text: Ask them to teach one lesson

effects.log: They teach one lesson, to your youngest disciple, which takes a minute, and which the disciple will be understanding for ten thousand years. (+8 prestige, +4 align)

events.text: Your old teacher, who became your disciple on the isle, has reached a gate they cannot pass: the realm above is closed to them, and their years are running out. They do not seem to mind. They ask only to spend what is left on your isle, teaching the youngest.

effects.log: They teach the youngest disciples the first stance, slowly and very well, until the end. The isle grieves them like a parent. (+8 prestige, +5 align)

choices.text: Try to carry them through the gate

effects.log: You pour years of your own qi into them. It is not enough, and they thank you for trying, and are not sorry. (+5 align, -10 health)

events.text: {npc}, the disciple who once spied on your isle for the Star Sea Pavilion, has become your envoy to every faction in the Upper Realm. {He} is, everyone agrees, the most trusted voice on the isle, precisely because {he} once was not.

effects.log: {npc} becomes the isle's first envoy, with a seal and a terrible hat. {He} wears the hat with great pride. (+6 prestige, +3 charm)
"That a place with nothing to hide is very frightening to everyone else," {npc} says. You think about that for years. (+5 Mind, +3 prestige)

events.text: {npc}, who passed the tribulation on your isle, now has a disciple of {his} own, whose storm is coming. {He} is standing at the cloud's edge beside the young one, very straight, trying not to look at you.

effects.log: You stay in the doorway, as you did once. {npc} glances back once, and you nod, and {he} turns to the storm. (+6 prestige, +4 align)

choices.text: Go and stand with them both

effects.log: Three of you under one storm. The storm, confused, comes down as warm rain. (+6 prestige, +4 charm)

events.text: {npc}, who found a Dao of {his} own on your isle, has decided to found an isle of {his} own. {He} comes to ask your leave, with a list of reasons so long it takes all afternoon to read.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Found a Dao

choices.text: Give your leave, and a gift

effects.log: You give {him} a cutting of the oldest pine on your isle. {His} isle drifts off at dawn, with the pine on it, and comes back to visit every century. (+8 prestige, +4 align)

choices.text: Ask {him} to wait one more century

effects.log: {npc} waits, and teaches, and leaves when the century is done, with your blessing and half your best disciples. (+5 prestige, +3 Mind)

events.text: The Tomb of the Nameless Emperor has stopped walking. It stopped, your maps say, the year you first went in and spoke to it, and it has been still ever since, the way a sleeper is still after a dream has been answered.

effects.log: The halls are quieter. On the coffin lid, under the dust, someone has drawn a small, crooked smile. (+5 Mind, +3 luck)
You burn them. The Tomb is where it is now, and will stay. (+4 align, +2 Mind)

events.text: Diving the Sea of Falling Stars again, years later, you find the drowned town's street empty of light. Every lantern has gone out, all at once, peacefully, as if the town had finally been told what it was waiting to hear, and gone to sleep.

effects.log: You light one lantern on the drowned street and leave it burning. It is still there, the divers say, a thousand years later. (+5 align, +3 Mind)
You leave the street dark. It is a good dark, the kind that comes after a long day. (+6 Mind)

events.text: Below, where the sea of clouds poured down as rain, there is a new country: a green land in the middle of what was desert, full of people who came for the water and stayed. They call the rain that made it the Heavens' Gift, and they hold a festival when it is cloudy.
events.arc: The Sinking of the Sea of Clouds

effects.log: You send a soft grey day over the new country. They dance in the streets, under umbrellas, for no reason they can name. (+6 align, +3 charm)
You watch the country grow for a century: its first city, its first quarrel, its first poem. (+6 Mind)

events.text: The dying star is a thing of the past now, one way or another, and the sailors below steer by it, or by its successor, without knowing. One of them, an old captain, has written a song about it, and the song has come up to you on the sea wind.

effects.log: You learn it. It is not very good and it is exactly right. You sing it on clear nights. (+5 charm, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Send the captain a fair wind

effects.log: The captain's last voyage has a fair wind the whole way. The song gets a new verse about it. (+6 align, +2 luck)

events.text: The stranger whose tribulation you shared has sent you something: a lightning-flower in a pot, from the place where the storm came down, and a note that says only: "When yours comes, I will be there."

choices.text: Keep the flower by your door

effects.log: It crackles softly by your door for a thousand years. When your next storm gathers, there is a figure at the edge of your isle, waiting. (+6 align, +3 luck)
You write back that the custom is broken now, and both of you are glad of it. You write to each other for ten thousand years. (+5 charm, +4 align)

events.text: An immortal younger than you, nervous, with a tribulation coming, has heard about your scar and has come to ask you, quietly, whether it hurt.

effects.log: "Yes," you say. "And then it hummed." The young immortal laughs, unexpectedly, and goes to the storm less afraid. (+6 align, +3 charm)
You show it. The young immortal looks a long time and says it is beautiful, which nobody has said before. (+5 charm, +4 Mind)

events.text: The silence you carry has become a thing people come to. Immortals with too much noise in their heads travel to wherever you are and sit near you for a while, and go away lighter. You did not intend it. You find you do not mind.

effects.log: They come for a century. You never say a word to most of them. They leave lighter every time. (+8 align, +3 Mind)

choices.text: Teach one of them to carry it too

effects.log: You teach one, a tired minister. Now there are two quiet places in the Upper Realm. (+6 Mind, +4 align)

events.text: One night in an ordinary storm the voice in the thunder says a number, and then it says: "Done." The old Sovereign who also hears it comes to your door at dawn, trembling, and you both wait to see what has changed.
events.arc: The Voice in the Last Bolt

effects.log: Nothing has changed. Then you notice: the storms are softer now, everywhere, for everyone. Heaven has finished counting, and is satisfied. (+10 Mind, +5 align)
You make tea and wait. By noon you are both laughing at how frightened you were, which, the Sovereign says, is what the number was for. (+6 Mind, +5 charm)
